rule MSSP_T1003_001_LSASS_Dump_File_After_Process_Open {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "Critical"
    description     = "Detects a non-system process opening a handle to lsass.exe (PROCESS_OPEN) followed within 10 minutes by creation of a minidump-style file on the same host. This two-stage sequence is characteristic of LSASS memory dumping via tools such as comsvcs.dll, procdump, or custom loaders, and is additive to existing command-line detections."
    mitre_tactic    = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1003.001"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR or Sysmon telemetry that emits PROCESS_OPEN events (Sysmon Event ID 10) and FILE_CREATION events. Both must be normalised into Chronicle UDM."
    platform        = "Windows"
    log_source      = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Legitimate crash-reporting tools (WER, Dr Watson), AV/EDR self-protection scanning lsass, authorised forensic tooling, backup agents. Tune using %lsass_open_allowed_processes and %lsass_dump_allowed_paths."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good parent process paths (e.g. EDR sensor binaries) to %lsass_open_allowed_processes. Add authorised dump output directories to %lsass_dump_allowed_paths. Consider narrowing the file extension regex if your environment never produces .dmp/.mdmp outside of WER."

  events:
    // Stage 1: a process opens a handle to lsass.exe
    $open.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_OPEN"
    $open.target.process.file.full_path = /\\lsass\.exe$/  nocase
    // Exclude well-known system paths that legitimately inspect lsass
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\windows\\system32\\(svchost|csrss|wininit|services|lsm)\.exe$/ nocase
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path in %lsass_open_allowed_processes
    $open.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Stage 2: a minidump-style file is created on the same host
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\.(dmp|mdmp|dump|bin)$/ nocase
    // Exclude the legitimate WER crash dump directory
    not $file.target.file.full_path = /\\windows\\(system32\\config\\systemprofile|minidump|temp\\wer)\\/ nocase
    not $file.target.file.full_path in %lsass_dump_allowed_paths
    $file.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Chronological ordering: handle open must precede file creation
    $open.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $file.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname over 10m

  outcome:
    $risk_score          = max(95)
    $mitre_technique_id  = array_distinct("T1003.001")
    $primary_entity      = array_distinct($hostname)
    $opening_process     = array_distinct($open.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $dump_file_path      = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $acting_user         = array_distinct($open.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $open and $file
}

rule MSSP_T1003_002_SAM_Registry_Hive_File_Creation {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "Critical"
    description = "Detects file creation events consistent with the SAM or SYSTEM registry hive being saved to disk outside of legitimate backup locations. Adversaries use 'reg save HKLM\\sam' or VSS shadow copy techniques to extract the SAM database for offline credential cracking. This rule fires on the resulting file artifact rather than the command line, providing coverage when process telemetry is suppressed or the attacker uses an alternative tool."
    mitre_tactic = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1003.002"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR or Sysmon file creation telemetry (Sysmon Event ID 11 or equivalent EDR file-write events normalised to UDM FILE_CREATION)."
    platform = "Windows"
    log_source = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Authorised backup software writing registry hives to a designated backup path, Windows in-box backup (wbadmin/NTBackup), domain join or provisioning tooling that legitimately exports hives."
    tuning_guidance = "Populate %global_allowed_hive_backup_paths with approved backup destination directories (e.g. your backup agent working directory). Populate %global_allowed_hive_writers with the full paths of authorised backup agent processes."

  events:
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"

    // Match files whose name looks like a raw SAM, SYSTEM, or SECURITY hive dump.
    // Covers: sam, sam.hive, sam.bak, sam.save, system, system.hive, security, security.hive, etc.
    // Also covers common attacker output names that include these keywords.
    (
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\\\/]sam(\.(hive|bak|save|dmp|bin|dat|old|copy|out|reg))?$/  nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\\\/]system(\.(hive|bak|save|dmp|bin|dat|old|copy|out|reg))?$/ nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\\\/]security(\.(hive|bak|save|dmp|bin|dat|old|copy|out|reg))?$/ nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /[\\\/]ntds(\.(hive|bak|save|dmp|bin|dat|old|copy|out|reg))?$/ nocase
    )

    // Exclude files written inside the canonical Windows registry store itself
    // (e.g. C:\Windows\System32\config\) - those are normal OS writes.
    not $file.target.file.full_path = /[Cc]:\\[Ww][Ii][Nn][Dd][Oo][Ww][Ss]\\[Ss]ystem32\\[Cc]onfig\\/

    // Exclude files written inside the Windows.old migration directory.
    not $file.target.file.full_path = /[Cc]:\\[Ww][Ii][Nn][Dd][Oo][Ww][Ss]\.old\\/

    // Exclude authorised backup destination paths defined per-client.
    not $file.target.file.full_path in %global_allowed_hive_backup_paths

    // Exclude authorised backup agent processes defined per-client.
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_hive_writers

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(90)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1003.002")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)
    $writing_process = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $hive_file_path = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $acting_user = array_distinct($file.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $file
}

rule MSSP_T1003_002_SAM_Registry_Export_Then_File_Creation {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "Critical"
    description = "Detects the two-stage SAM database extraction pattern: a process opens a handle to the HKLM\\SAM or HKLM\\SYSTEM registry hive (registry read/modification event), followed within 10 minutes by creation of a suspicious output file on the same host. This covers reg.exe save, Volume Shadow Copy access, and other in-memory dump tools that write the SAM hive to disk without relying on command-line string matching."
    mitre_tactic = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1003.002"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR or Sysmon registry telemetry (Event ID 12/13 or equivalent UDM REGISTRY_MODIFICATION) and file-creation telemetry (Sysmon Event ID 11 or EDR equivalent). Both event types must be normalised into Chronicle UDM."
    platform = "Windows"
    log_source = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Backup software performing authorised registry exports, Windows built-in repair/recovery operations, domain join or provisioning tooling that reads the SAM hive, authorised IT asset-management agents."
    tuning_guidance = "Add authorised backup or provisioning process paths to %global_allowed_sam_readers. Add known-safe output directories (e.g. backup share mount points) to %global_allowed_sam_output_paths. Scope by hostname or OU tag for servers where backup jobs are expected."

  events:
    // Stage 1: A process touches the SAM or SYSTEM registry hive.
    // Covers reg save, VSS-based readers, and in-memory tools that
    // open the hive key before dumping it.
    $reg.metadata.event_type = "REGISTRY_MODIFICATION"
    $reg.target.registry.registry_key = /\\(SAM|SYSTEM|SECURITY)(\\.+)?$/ nocase
    $reg.target.registry.registry_key = /^HKLM/ nocase
    not $reg.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_sam_readers
    $reg.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Stage 2: A file is created whose name or path suggests a SAM/SYSTEM
    // hive dump. Matches common output names used by reg save, secretsdump,
    // and similar tooling without hardcoding tool names.
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"
    (
      $file.target.file.full_path = /\\(sam|system|security|ntds|hklm)(\.hiv|\.save|\.bak|\.dmp|\.bin|\.dat)?$/  nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /\\(dump|creds|hashes|loot)\b/ nocase
    )
    not $file.target.file.full_path in %global_allowed_sam_output_paths
    $file.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Chronological ordering: registry access precedes file creation
    $reg.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $file.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname over 10m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(95)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1003.002")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($hostname)
    $reg_keys_accessed = array_distinct($reg.target.registry.registry_key)
    $dumping_processes = array_distinct($reg.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $output_files_created = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $file_creating_processes = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)

  condition:
    $reg and $file
}

rule MSSP_T1003_003_NTDS_File_Access_Outside_System_Directory {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "Critical"
    description = "Detects creation or modification of NTDS.dit database file outside its protected system directory, indicating extraction of Active Directory credential database."
    mitre_tactic = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1003.003"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping: NTDS"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR file telemetry or Windows file auditing."
    platform = "Windows"
    log_source = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Legitimate AD database backups, domain controller migration activities, authorized forensic investigations, backup software with AD-aware agents."
    tuning_guidance = "Add approved backup tool process paths to %global_allowed_backup_processes. Exclude authorized backup destinations via %global_allowed_backup_paths."

  events:
    ($file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION" or $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_MODIFICATION")
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\\ntds\.dit$/ nocase
    not $file.target.file.full_path = /^[a-z]:\\windows\\ntds\\ntds\.dit$/ nocase
    not $file.target.file.full_path = /^[a-z]:\\windows\\system32\\ntds\.dit$/ nocase
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_backup_processes
    not $file.target.file.full_path in %global_allowed_backup_paths

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(95)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1003.003")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)

  condition:
    $file
}

rule MSSP_T1003_003_NTDS_ShadowCopy_Then_NTDS_File_Creation {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "Critical"
    description     = "Detects a two-stage NTDS extraction pattern: (1) a Volume Shadow Copy is created or accessed via vssadmin, wmic, or diskshadow, followed within 10 minutes by (2) a file-creation event whose path contains ntds.dit outside the canonical NTDS directory. This covers shadow-copy-based NTDS theft without relying on command-line string matching already covered by existing rules."
    mitre_tactic    = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1003.003"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping: NTDS"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR or Sysmon file-creation telemetry (Event ID 11) and process-launch telemetry (Event ID 1 / equivalent EDR). Both event types must be ingested and normalised to UDM."
    platform        = "Windows"
    log_source      = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Authorised backup agents (Veeam, Commvault, Windows Server Backup) that legitimately snapshot AD data; DR test procedures; AD migration tooling. Tune using %global_allowed_backup_processes."
    tuning_guidance = "Add the full path of authorised backup agent executables to %global_allowed_backup_processes. If the environment uses a non-default NTDS path, adjust the ntds\.dit regex accordingly. Consider scoping to Domain Controller hostnames via a reference list %dc_hostnames."

  events:
    // Stage 1 – VSS / shadow-copy invocation
    $vss.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_LAUNCH"
    $vss.target.process.file.full_path = /\\(vssadmin|wmic|diskshadow|wbadmin)\.exe$/ nocase
    (
        $vss.target.process.command_line = /shadow/ nocase or
        $vss.target.process.command_line = /shadowcopy/ nocase or
        $vss.target.process.command_line = /shadowstorage/ nocase or
        $vss.target.process.command_line = /backup/ nocase
    )
    not $vss.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_backup_processes
    $vss.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Stage 2 – ntds.dit file appears outside its canonical location
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"
    $file.target.file.full_path = /ntds\.dit/ nocase
    not $file.target.file.full_path = /\\Windows\\NTDS\\Ntds\.dit$/ nocase
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_backup_processes
    $file.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Chronological ordering: shadow copy first, file creation second
    $vss.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $file.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname over 10m

  outcome:
    $risk_score          = max(95)
    $mitre_technique_id  = array_distinct("T1003.003")
    $primary_entity      = array_distinct($hostname)
    $shadow_process      = array_distinct($vss.target.process.file.full_path)
    $shadow_cmdline      = array_distinct($vss.target.process.command_line)
    $ntds_copy_path      = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $initiating_process  = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)

  condition:
    $vss and $file
}

rule MSSP_T1003_004_LSA_Secrets_Registry_Access {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "Critical"
    description = "Detects registry read or modification access to HKLM\\SECURITY\\Policy\\Secrets, the storage location for LSA secrets. Legitimate access to this key is extremely rare outside of the SYSTEM account performing internal OS operations. Adversaries with SYSTEM privileges use tools such as Mimikatz or reg.exe to extract service account credentials, cached domain credentials, and other sensitive material stored under this key."
    mitre_tactic = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1003.004"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping: LSA Secrets"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR or Sysmon registry telemetry (Sysmon Event ID 12/13/14 or equivalent EDR registry events) normalised into Chronicle UDM REGISTRY_MODIFICATION or REGISTRY_CREATION events. Registry auditing must be enabled for HKLM\\SECURITY."
    platform = "Windows"
    log_source = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Windows LSASS performing internal credential refresh; backup agents running as SYSTEM that snapshot the registry hive; some endpoint security products that audit LSA secrets as part of credential hygiene checks."
    tuning_guidance = "Add trusted SYSTEM-level security or backup process paths to %lsa_secrets_allowed_processes. If noise persists, further scope by requiring the accessing process to NOT be lsass.exe or services.exe, which are the only legitimate callers under normal OS operation."

  events:
    $reg.metadata.event_type = "REGISTRY_MODIFICATION"
    $reg.target.registry.registry_key = /\\HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\SECURITY\\Policy\\Secrets/ nocase
    not $reg.principal.process.file.full_path in %lsa_secrets_allowed_processes
    not $reg.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\lsass\.exe$/ nocase
    not $reg.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\services\.exe$/ nocase
    not $reg.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\svchost\.exe$/ nocase

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(90)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1003.004")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($reg.principal.hostname)
    $accessing_process = array_distinct($reg.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $registry_key_accessed = array_distinct($reg.target.registry.registry_key)
    $acting_user = array_distinct($reg.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $reg
}

rule MSSP_T1003_004_LSA_Secrets_Registry_Access_Then_File_Drop {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "Critical"
    description = "Detects a process opening the HKLM\\SECURITY\\Policy\\Secrets registry hive followed by a file creation event from the same process on the same host within 10 minutes. This two-stage pattern is consistent with LSA secret extraction tools that read the registry and then write credentials to disk for exfiltration. Variant 2 of 2 for T1003.004 - complements the process command-line rule with a registry-read-to-file-drop correlation."
    mitre_tactic = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1003.004"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping: LSA Secrets"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR or Sysmon telemetry producing REGISTRY_MODIFICATION or REGISTRY_CREATION events for HKLM\\SECURITY\\Policy\\Secrets and FILE_CREATION events. Sysmon Event IDs 12/13 (registry) and 11 (file create) are sufficient. The SECURITY hive is ACL-protected; only SYSTEM-level processes can access it, so false-positive volume is inherently low."
    platform = "Windows"
    log_source = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Authorised backup agents (e.g. Windows Server Backup, VSS writers) that snapshot the SECURITY hive. Domain-join or GPO-refresh operations on domain controllers. Legitimate credential-management utilities run by the security team."
    tuning_guidance = "Add authorised backup or credential-management process paths to %global_allowed_lsa_readers. Add known-safe output directories (e.g. VSS staging paths) to %global_allowed_lsa_output_paths. On DCs, consider raising the match window or adding a DC hostname exclusion list."

  events:
    // Event 1: A process touches the LSA Secrets registry path.
    // REGISTRY_MODIFICATION is used because EDR/Sysmon commonly surfaces
    // SYSTEM-level registry access as a modification event on this protected hive.
    $reg.metadata.event_type = "REGISTRY_MODIFICATION"
    $reg.target.registry.registry_key = /\\SECURITY\\Policy\\Secrets/ nocase
    not $reg.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_lsa_readers
    $reg.principal.hostname = $hostname
    $reg.principal.process.file.full_path = $proc_path

    // Event 2: The same process (matched by path) creates a file on the same host.
    // Credential dumpers write secrets to a staging file before exfiltration.
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"
    $file.principal.hostname = $hostname
    $file.principal.process.file.full_path = $proc_path
    not $file.target.file.full_path in %global_allowed_lsa_output_paths
    // Exclude well-known benign write destinations to reduce noise
    not $file.target.file.full_path = /\\Windows\\(WinSxS|SoftwareDistribution|Temp\\MpCmdRun)/ nocase
    not $file.target.file.full_path = /\\Windows\\System32\\(winevt|sru|catroot)/ nocase

    // Chronological ordering: registry access must precede file creation
    $reg.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $file.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname, $proc_path over 10m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(92)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1003.004")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($reg.principal.hostname)
    $offending_process = array_distinct($proc_path)
    $registry_keys_accessed = array_distinct($reg.target.registry.registry_key)
    $files_created = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $principal_user = array_distinct($reg.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $reg and $file
}

rule MSSP_T1003_005_Linux_Cached_Domain_Cred_DB_Access {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Single-Event"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects file-read or open access to Linux cached domain credential databases maintained by SSSD or Quest Authentication Services. Adversaries with elevated privileges read these LDB/VDB files to extract cached domain credential hashes for offline cracking. This rule fires on the file artifact access rather than the command line used to trigger it, providing coverage that survives tool renaming or obfuscated invocations."
    mitre_tactic    = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1003.005"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping: Cached Domain Credentials"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires Linux EDR or auditd file-open/read telemetry normalised to Chronicle UDM FILE_READ events. Auditd rules must include '-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S open,openat -F path=/var/lib/sss/db -F perm=r' and equivalent for /var/opt/quest/vas/authcache/."
    platform        = "Linux"
    log_source      = "linux_endpoint"
    false_positives = "SSSD daemon itself performing routine cache reads, sssd_be and sssd_nss processes, Quest VAS daemon (vasd), authorised identity management tooling, backup agents reading /var/lib/sss/db as part of a scheduled backup."
    tuning_guidance = "Add trusted process paths (e.g. /usr/sbin/sssd, /opt/quest/sbin/vasd, backup agent binaries) to %linux_allowed_credential_cache_readers. Scope further by excluding known service accounts in $open.principal.user.userid."

  events:
    $open.metadata.event_type = "FILE_READ"

    // Target the SSSD cache LDB files or Quest VAS auth cache VDB files
    // These are the canonical on-disk locations for Linux cached domain credentials
    $open.target.file.full_path = /^\/var\/lib\/sss\/db\/cache\.[^\/]+\.ldb$/ nocase or
    $open.target.file.full_path = /^\/var\/lib\/sss\/db\/ccache_/ nocase or
    $open.target.file.full_path = /^\/var\/opt\/quest\/vas\/authcache\/vas_auth\.vdb$/ nocase or
    $open.target.file.full_path = /^\/var\/opt\/quest\/vas\/authcache\// nocase

    // Exclude the legitimate daemons that own these files
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path in %linux_allowed_credential_cache_readers

    // Exclude root-owned system service processes by name pattern where path is populated
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\/(sssd|sssd_be|sssd_nss|sssd_pam|sssd_kcm|vasd|vastool)$/ nocase

  outcome:
    $risk_score        = max(80)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1003.005")
    $primary_entity    = array_distinct($open.principal.hostname)
    $accessing_process = array_distinct($open.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $accessing_user    = array_distinct($open.principal.user.userid)
    $accessed_file     = array_distinct($open.target.file.full_path)

  condition:
    $open
}

rule MSSP_T1003_005_Registry_Access_Then_LSASS_Read {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "Critical"
    description = "Detects registry access to cached credential configuration followed by LSASS process handle acquisition, indicating potential cached domain credential extraction."
    mitre_tactic = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1003.005"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping: Cached Domain Credentials"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR process and registry telemetry with handle tracking."
    platform = "Windows"
    log_source = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Security scanning tools, credential management utilities, system diagnostics, backup software accessing registry hives."
    tuning_guidance = "Add approved security tools to %global_allowed_credential_tools. Exclude known admin workstations via %global_admin_workstations."

  events:
    $reg.metadata.event_type = "REGISTRY_MODIFICATION"
    $reg.target.registry.registry_key = /\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Lsa\\(CachedLogonsCount|DisableDomainCreds)/ nocase
    not $reg.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_credential_tools
    $reg.principal.hostname = $hostname
    $reg.principal.user.userid = $userid

    $open.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_OPEN"
    $open.target.process.file.full_path = /\\lsass\.exe$/ nocase
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\(MsMpEng|SenseIR|csagent|elastic-agent)\.exe$/ nocase
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_credential_tools
    $open.principal.hostname = $hostname
    $open.principal.user.userid = $userid

    $reg.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $open.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname, $userid over 10m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(95)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1003.005")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($open.principal.hostname)
    $suspicious_process = array_distinct($open.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $registry_keys_accessed = array_distinct($reg.target.registry.registry_key)
    $user_context = array_distinct($open.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $reg and $open
}

rule MSSP_T1003_006_DCSync_Network_Replication_Traffic {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "Critical"
    description = "Detects network-observable DCSync behaviour: an unexpected host initiating MS-DRSR (Directory Replication Service Remote Protocol) connections to a Domain Controller on port 135 (RPC endpoint mapper) or high RPC ports (49152-65535) that are characteristic of DRSUAPI replication traffic. Legitimate AD replication originates only from known Domain Controllers. Traffic from non-DC hosts to DC RPC ports is a strong indicator of DCSync credential dumping."
    mitre_tactic = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1003.006"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping: DCSync"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires firewall or network perimeter flow logs with source/destination IP and port visibility. Internal DC IP ranges must be maintained in %dc_ip_ranges reference list. Known-good replication sources (legitimate DCs) must be maintained in %known_dc_sources."
    platform = "Windows"
    log_source = "firewall"
    false_positives = "Legitimate Domain Controller replication traffic if DC source IPs are not fully enumerated in %known_dc_sources. Azure AD Connect or third-party directory sync tools performing legitimate replication. Vulnerability scanners probing RPC ports. Backup agents with AD integration."
    tuning_guidance = "Populate %known_dc_sources with all Domain Controller IP addresses in the environment. Populate %dc_ip_ranges with all subnets hosting Domain Controllers. Add Azure AD Connect server IPs and approved directory sync appliances to %known_dc_sources. Consider narrowing to port 135 only if high-port RPC generates excessive noise."

  events:
    $net.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_CONNECTION"

    // Traffic destined for a known Domain Controller
    $net.target.ip in %dc_ip_ranges

    // RPC endpoint mapper (DCSync initiates here) or dynamic RPC high ports used by DRSUAPI
    (
      $net.target.port = 135 or
      ($net.target.port >= 49152 and $net.target.port <= 65535)
    )

    // Source is NOT a known legitimate Domain Controller performing replication
    not $net.principal.ip in %known_dc_sources

    // Source is NOT excluded as an approved directory sync tool or admin host
    not $net.principal.ip in %approved_dirsync_hosts

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(85)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1003.006")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($net.principal.ip)
    $destination_dc = array_distinct($net.target.ip)
    $destination_port = array_distinct($net.target.port)

  condition:
    $net
}

rule MSSP_T1003_006_DCSync_Network_Replication_Sequence {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "Critical"
    description = "Detects DCSync attacks by correlating anomalous DRSUAPI/MS-DRSR replication traffic observed by an IDS/IPS sensor. A non-domain-controller host initiating replication-protocol connections to a DC on port 135 (RPC endpoint mapper) followed by high-port RPC callbacks is characteristic of DCSync credential dumping. The rule joins two network flow events over a 10-minute window on the source host, requiring both the initial RPC bind and the subsequent dynamic RPC channel, while excluding known-legitimate DC-to-DC replication pairs."
    mitre_tactic = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1003.006"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping: DCSync"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires IDS/IPS or network security appliance logs normalised to Chronicle UDM NETWORK_CONNECTION or NETWORK_FLOW events. The sensor must inspect east-west traffic between endpoints and domain controllers. Port 135 (RPC EPM) and dynamic high-port RPC flows must be visible."
    platform = "Windows"
    log_source = "ips"
    false_positives = "Legitimate domain controller replication (SYSVOL, AD replication between DCs), backup agents performing AD snapshots, Azure AD Connect sync hosts, legitimate identity governance tools querying AD via RPC."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known DC-to-DC replication source IPs to %dc_replication_sources. Add authorised AD sync tool hosts to %global_allowed_ad_sync_hosts. Narrow the high-port range if the environment uses a fixed RPC port range via Group Policy."

  events:
    // Event 1: Source host contacts a DC on TCP 135 (RPC Endpoint Mapper)
    // This is the first step of a DCSync: the attacker resolves the DRSUAPI endpoint.
    $rpc_bind.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_CONNECTION"
    $rpc_bind.target.port = 135
    $rpc_bind.network.ip_protocol = "TCP"
    not $rpc_bind.principal.ip in %dc_replication_sources
    not $rpc_bind.principal.ip in %global_allowed_ad_sync_hosts
    $rpc_bind.principal.ip = $src_ip

    // Event 2: Same source host opens a dynamic high-port RPC channel to the same DC
    // shortly after. DCSync uses the dynamic port returned by the EPM to stream
    // directory replication data (MS-DRSR GetNCChanges).
    $rpc_data.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_CONNECTION"
    $rpc_data.target.port >= 49152
    $rpc_data.target.port <= 65535
    $rpc_data.network.ip_protocol = "TCP"
    // The dynamic RPC channel must go to the same destination as the EPM query
    $rpc_data.target.ip = $rpc_bind.target.ip
    not $rpc_data.principal.ip in %dc_replication_sources
    not $rpc_data.principal.ip in %global_allowed_ad_sync_hosts
    $rpc_data.principal.ip = $src_ip

    // Enforce chronological ordering: EPM query must precede the data channel
    $rpc_bind.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $rpc_data.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $src_ip over 10m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(90)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1003.006")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($src_ip)
    $destination_dc_ips = array_distinct($rpc_data.target.ip)
    $dynamic_ports_observed = array_distinct($rpc_data.target.port)

  condition:
    $rpc_bind and $rpc_data
}

rule MSSP_T1003_007_Proc_Mem_Maps_File_Read {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Single-Event"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects file-read access to /proc/<PID>/mem or /proc/<PID>/maps for a process other than the reader's own PID. Adversaries with root privileges open these pseudo-files to extract credentials from another process's virtual address space without spawning a dedicated dump utility. This rule fires on the FILE_READ artifact produced by the kernel when the file descriptor is opened, providing coverage that is orthogonal to command-line process-creation rules."
    mitre_tactic         = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique      = "T1003.007"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping: Proc Filesystem"
    log_prerequisites    = "Requires Linux EDR or auditd with file-read (open/openat) syscall auditing enabled for /proc/<PID>/mem and /proc/<PID>/maps. Auditd rule example: -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S open,openat -F dir=/proc -F exit=-EACCES -k proc_mem_access"
    platform         = "Linux"
    log_source       = "linux_endpoint"
    false_positives  = "Debuggers (gdb, lldb, strace), legitimate memory profilers (valgrind, perf), Java/JVM garbage-collection introspection, container runtimes reading their own process maps, security scanners, and some monitoring agents."
    tuning_guidance  = "Add trusted profiling and debugging tool paths to %linux_allowed_proc_readers. Scope further by requiring the reading process UID to be 0 (root) if your EDR surfaces that field. Consider excluding known container runtime paths such as /usr/bin/containerd or /usr/bin/runc."

  events:
    $open.metadata.event_type = "FILE_READ"

    // Target must be a /proc/<numeric-PID>/mem or /proc/<numeric-PID>/maps path.
    // The numeric PID segment ensures we skip /proc/self/*, /proc/net/*, etc.
    $open.target.file.full_path = /^\/proc\/[0-9]+\/(mem|maps)$/ nocase

    // The reading process must not be a kernel thread (no file path) and must
    // have a resolvable executable path on the filesystem.
    $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /^\// nocase

    // Exclude processes reading their own /proc/<own-PID>/ entry.
    // EDRs that populate both fields allow this self-read exclusion.
    // When the fields are absent the rule still fires on cross-PID reads.
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /^\/(proc\/self|proc\/[0-9]+\/exe)$/ nocase

    // Exclude known-safe profiling and debugging tools via reference list.
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path in %linux_allowed_proc_readers

    // Exclude common benign parent paths (kernel workers, systemd service managers).
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\/(systemd|journald|auditd|sshd)$/ nocase

  outcome:
    $risk_score        = max(80)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1003.007")
    $primary_entity    = array_distinct($open.principal.hostname)
    $reading_process   = array_distinct($open.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $target_proc_file  = array_distinct($open.target.file.full_path)
    $actor_userid      = array_distinct($open.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $open
}

rule MSSP_T1003_007_Proc_Mem_Read_Then_File_Write {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects a process opening /proc/<PID>/mem or /proc/<PID>/maps for reading (credential scraping from virtual memory) followed within 10 minutes by a file write to a world-writable or temp-like directory on the same host. This two-stage pattern — read process memory, then stage output — is characteristic of in-memory credential dumpers such as MimiPenguin and similar tools targeting Linux process memory."
    mitre_tactic    = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1003.007"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping: Proc Filesystem"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires Linux EDR or auditd telemetry normalised to Chronicle UDM. FILE_READ events must be generated for /proc/<PID>/mem and /proc/<PID>/maps access. FILE_CREATION events must be generated for writes to /tmp, /dev/shm, /var/tmp, or similar staging paths."
    platform        = "Linux"
    log_source      = "linux_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Legitimate debuggers (gdb, strace, ltrace) reading /proc/<PID>/mem; performance monitoring tools reading /proc/<PID>/maps; crash reporters (Breakpad, Crashpad); container runtimes inspecting child process memory; security scanners."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good parent process paths (e.g. gdb, strace, crash reporter binaries) to %linux_allowed_proc_mem_readers. Add approved staging directories to %linux_allowed_staging_paths. Consider narrowing the file write side to non-root users if your environment's legitimate debuggers run as root."

  events:
    // Stage 1: process reads /proc/<PID>/mem or /proc/<PID>/maps
    $read.metadata.event_type = "FILE_READ"
    $read.target.file.full_path = /\/proc\/[0-9]+\/(mem|maps)$/ nocase
    not $read.principal.process.file.full_path in %linux_allowed_proc_mem_readers
    $read.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Stage 2: same host writes a file to a world-writable / staging path
    $write.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"
    $write.target.file.full_path = /^\/(tmp|dev\/shm|var\/tmp|run\/shm)\// nocase
    not $write.target.file.full_path in %linux_allowed_staging_paths
    $write.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Chronological ordering: memory read must precede the staged file write
    $read.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $write.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname over 10m

  outcome:
    $risk_score        = max(85)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1003.007")
    $primary_entity    = array_distinct($read.principal.hostname)
    $reading_process   = array_distinct($read.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $proc_paths_read   = array_distinct($read.target.file.full_path)
    $staged_files      = array_distinct($write.target.file.full_path)
    $writing_user      = array_distinct($write.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $read and $write
}

rule MSSP_T1003_001_LSASS_Handle_Request {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Single-Event"
    severity        = "Critical"
    description     = "Detects a non-system process opening a handle to lsass.exe with access rights consistent with memory reading (credential dumping). Attackers must open a handle to lsass to extract credentials from its memory; this is the OS-level state change that cannot be hidden by renaming a tool or clearing command-line logs."
    mitre_tactic    = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1003"
    mitre_technique_name = "OS Credential Dumping"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR or Sysmon (Event ID 10 - ProcessAccess) telemetry normalised into UDM PROCESS_OPEN events. The sensor must capture target.process.file.full_path and principal.process.file.full_path for handle-open events."
    platform        = "Windows"
    log_source      = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "AV/EDR agents performing self-protection checks, Windows Task Manager (taskmgr.exe), Process Explorer (sysinternals), authorised vulnerability scanners, WerFault.exe crash handling, and some backup agents that enumerate process memory."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good security tooling and admin utilities to %global_lsass_handle_allowlist by their full path. Consider also suppressing alerts where principal.process.file.full_path matches your deployed EDR sensor path. Raise severity threshold if the opening process is unsigned or running from a user-writable directory."

  events:
    $open.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_OPEN"

    // Target must be lsass.exe - the credential store process
    $open.target.process.file.full_path = /\\lsass\.exe$/ nocase

    // Exclude the process opening itself (lsass self-reference during init)
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\lsass\.exe$/ nocase

    // Exclude core OS processes that legitimately access lsass
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\(System32|SysWOW64)\\(wininit|services|svchost|csrss|smss|werfault|wermgr|taskhostw|lsm)\.exe$/ nocase

    // Exclude known Windows security and management binaries
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\(System32|SysWOW64)\\(taskmgr|mmc|perfmon|resmon|rdrleakdiag|audiodg)\.exe$/ nocase

    // well-known system components (broad OS path anchor)
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /^[Cc]:\\[Ww][Ii][Nn][Dd][Oo][Ww][Ss]\\[Ss][Yy][Ss][Tt][Ee][Mm]32\\[Ww][Ee][Rr]/ nocase

    // Customer-managed allowlist for authorised security tooling
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_lsass_handle_allowlist

    // Require a non-empty opening process path (filters noise / incomplete telemetry)
    $open.principal.process.file.full_path != ""

    // Capture the opening process path for outcome enrichment
    $open.principal.process.file.full_path = $opener_path

  outcome:
    $risk_score        = max(90)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1003")
    $primary_entity    = array_distinct($open.principal.hostname)
    $opening_process   = array_distinct($opener_path)
    $target_process    = array_distinct($open.target.process.file.full_path)
    $affected_user     = array_distinct($open.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $open
}

    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects a two-stage DLL injection pattern: a suspicious DLL dropped into a writable system or user path, followed within 5 minutes by a non-standard process opening a handle to a high-value target process (PROCESS_OPEN). This covers the WriteProcessMemory + CreateRemoteThread injection pattern without relying on command-line matching."
    mitre_tactic    = "Defense Evasion, Privilege Escalation"
    mitre_technique = "T1055.001"
    mitre_technique_name = "Process Injection: Dynamic-link Library Injection"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR or Sysmon telemetry normalised to UDM. FILE_CREATION events for DLL drops and PROCESS_OPEN events for cross-process handle acquisition must both be present. Sysmon Event IDs 11 (FileCreate) and 10 (ProcessAccess) are the primary sources."
    platform        = "Windows"
    log_source      = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Legitimate software installers dropping DLLs and then loading them into a host process; AV/EDR products performing self-injection for hooking; JIT compilers (JVM, .NET CLR) writing and loading temporary DLLs; software update agents."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good installer or updater parent process paths to %global_allowed_dll_writers. Add known-good processes that legitimately open handles to lsass or other sensitive targets to %global_allowed_process_openers. Narrow the DLL drop path regex if your environment uses a specific staging directory."

  events:
    // Stage 1: A DLL is written to a writable path that is not a standard
    // software installation directory. Covers temp, user-profile, and
    // ProgramData staging locations commonly used by injectors.
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\.(dll)$/ nocase
    $file.target.file.full_path = /(\\Temp\\|\\AppData\\|\\ProgramData\\|\\Users\\[^\\]+\\)/ nocase
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_dll_writers
    $file.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Stage 2: A process opens a handle to a sensitive target process.
    // PROCESS_OPEN is the UDM event type for cross-process handle acquisition
    // (Sysmon Event ID 10 / EDR equivalent). We filter to processes opening
    // high-value targets: lsass, svchost, explorer, winlogon, services.
    $open.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_OPEN"
    $open.target.process.file.full_path = /(\\lsass\.exe|\\svchost\.exe|\\explorer\.exe|\\winlogon\.exe|\\services\.exe)$/ nocase
    // The opener must NOT itself be a known-good system process
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /(\\MsMpEng\.exe|\\csrss\.exe|\\wininit\.exe|\\System32\\svchost\.exe)$/ nocase
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_process_openers
    $open.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Chronological ordering: DLL drop must precede the process open
    $file.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $open.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score          = max(85)
    $mitre_technique_id  = array_distinct("T1055.001")
    $primary_entity      = array_distinct($hostname)
    $dropped_dll_paths   = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $injector_process    = array_distinct($open.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $target_process      = array_distinct($open.target.process.file.full_path)
    $writing_process     = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)

  condition:
    $file and $open
}

rule MSSP_T1055_003_Thread_Hijack_Process_Handle_Open {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Single-Event"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects a non-system process opening a handle to a remote thread-ownable process with the access rights required for Thread Execution Hijacking (THREAD_SUSPEND_RESUME | THREAD_SET_CONTEXT | THREAD_GET_CONTEXT combined with PROCESS_VM_WRITE / PROCESS_VM_OPERATION).     mitre_technique = "T1055.003"
    mitre_technique_name = "Process Injection: Thread Execution Hijacking"

rule MSSP_T1055_003_ThreadHijack_OpenThenAnomalousChild {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects thread execution hijacking by correlating a non-standard process opening a handle to a remote process (PROCESS_OPEN) followed by that same process spawning an unexpected child within a short window. Thread hijacking requires OpenThread/SuspendThread/WriteProcessMemory/ResumeThread; the injecting process typically opens a victim process handle and then the victim process (or the injector itself) launches a child that is inconsistent with its normal lineage. This rule joins the handle-open event to a subsequent child process launch where the parent is a known-legitimate host process being abused as an injection target."
    mitre_tactic    = "Defense Evasion, Privilege Escalation"
    mitre_technique = "T1055.003"
    mitre_technique_name = "Process Injection: Thread Execution Hijacking"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR or Sysmon telemetry that emits PROCESS_OPEN events (Sysmon Event ID 10 / EDR equivalent) and PROCESS_LAUNCH events with parent process lineage populated."
    platform        = "Windows"
    log_source      = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Legitimate debuggers (Visual Studio, WinDbg), AV/EDR self-protection, JIT compilers (JVM, CLR), RMM agents that inspect running processes."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-safe opener binaries to %global_allowed_process_openers. Add approved parent-child pairs to %global_allowed_injection_parents. Narrow the target process list if the environment has a well-defined baseline."

  events:
    // Event 1: A non-standard process opens a handle to a well-known host process
    // that is a common injection target (svchost, explorer, lsass, etc.)
    $open.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_OPEN"
    // The opener must NOT be a known-safe administrative or security tool
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_process_openers
    // The opener must not itself be a Windows system binary in System32
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\Windows\\System32\\/ nocase
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\/ nocase
    // Target of the open must be a commonly hijacked host process
    $open.target.process.file.full_path = /\\(svchost|explorer|lsass|spoolsv|winlogon|csrss|services|taskhost|taskhostw|dllhost|rundll32|regsvr32|msiexec)\.exe$/ nocase
    // Bind the hostname for the join
    $open.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Event 2: Within the window, the same host process (injection target) spawns
    // a child process that is anomalous for that parent — a shell, script engine,
    // or reconnaissance binary
    $proc.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_LAUNCH"
    // Parent is the same well-known host process that was targeted above
    $proc.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\(svchost|explorer|lsass|spoolsv|winlogon|csrss|services|taskhost|taskhostw|dllhost|rundll32|regsvr32|msiexec)\.exe$/ nocase
    // Child is a shell, script engine, or common post-exploitation binary
    $proc.target.process.file.full_path = /\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta|certutil|bitsadmin|regsvr32|rundll32|wmic|net|whoami|ipconfig|nltest|ping|nslookup|curl|wget)\.exe$/ nocase
    not $proc.target.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_injection_parents
    $proc.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Chronological ordering: handle open must precede the child launch
    $open.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $proc.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score          = max(85)
    $mitre_technique_id  = array_distinct("T1055.003")
    $primary_entity      = array_distinct($hostname)
    $opener_process      = array_distinct($open.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $hijacked_host       = array_distinct($open.target.process.file.full_path)
    $spawned_child       = array_distinct($proc.target.process.file.full_path)
    $child_cmdline       = array_distinct($proc.target.process.command_line)
    $open_event_count    = count($open.metadata.id)

  condition:
    $open and $proc
}

rule MSSP_T1055_004_APC_Injection_Suspended_Process_Handle {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Single-Event"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects PROCESS_OPEN events where a process requests cross-process handle access consistent with APC injection preparation: a non-system process opens a handle to a remote process with VM_WRITE and/or THREAD access rights.     platform        = "Windows"
    log_source      = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Debuggers (Visual Studio, WinDbg), legitimate AV/EDR self-protection, process monitoring tools (Process Hacker, Sysinternals), JIT compilers, and some game anti-cheat engines open remote process handles with broad rights."

  events:

    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\Windows\\System32\\/  nocase
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\/ nocase
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\Windows\\WinSxS\\/   nocase

    // Exclude approved administrative and security tooling via reference list
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_process_openers

    $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\(Users|AppData|ProgramData|Temp|Downloads|Desktop)\\/i nocase

    $open.principal.process.pid != $open.target.process.pid

    // (Chronicle populates target.process.file.full_path for the victim process)

    $open.principal.process.file.full_path != ""

  outcome:

    $opener_pid        = array_distinct($open.principal.process.pid)
    $target_pid        = array_distinct($open.target.process.pid)

rule MSSP_T1055_004_APC_Injection_Suspended_Process_Then_Remote_Open {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects the Early Bird APC injection pattern: a non-standard parent process creates a suspended child process (first event), followed by a cross-process PROCESS_OPEN from the same parent targeting a different process (second event). This two-stage sequence is characteristic of APC injection where a suspended process is created, malicious code is written into it, and QueueUserAPC is used to execute it before the entry point. Variant 2 of 2 for T1055.004 - focuses on process-open telemetry rather than command-line matching."
    mitre_tactic = "Defense Evasion, Privilege Escalation"
    mitre_technique = "T1055.004"
    mitre_technique_name = "Process Injection: Asynchronous Procedure Call"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR or Sysmon telemetry producing PROCESS_LAUNCH events with command-line arguments and PROCESS_OPEN events with cross-process handle acquisition. Sysmon Event IDs 1 and 10 map to these UDM types."
    platform = "Windows"
    log_source = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Debuggers (WinDbg, x64dbg), legitimate software installers that spawn suspended helper processes, JIT compilers, and some AV/EDR products that inject into processes for monitoring. Tune using %global_allowed_suspended_process_parents."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good parent process paths (e.g. installer frameworks, debuggers, JIT engines) to %global_allowed_suspended_process_parents. Consider narrowing the child process filter to exclude well-known system utilities if noise is high."

  events:
    // First event: a process launches a child with the CREATE_SUSPENDED flag
    // visible in the command line or via EDR-enriched fields.
    // Narrow pre-filter: exclude common benign parents and require the
    // suspended-creation indicator that EDR/Sysmon surfaces.
    $launch.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_LAUNCH"
    $launch.target.process.command_line = /\-suspended|\bcreatesuspended\b|CREATE_SUSPENDED/ nocase
    not $launch.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\(msiexec|setup|install|update|windbg|devenv|rider|clion|idea64|eclipse)\.exe$/ nocase
    not $launch.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_suspended_process_parents
    $launch.principal.hostname = $hostname
    $launch.principal.process.file.full_path = $parent_path

    // Second event: the same parent process (or a process on the same host
    // with the same image path) opens a handle to another process.
    // PROCESS_OPEN is the UDM event type for cross-process handle acquisition
    // (Sysmon Event ID 10 / EDR equivalent).
    $open.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_OPEN"
    $open.principal.process.file.full_path = $parent_path
    $open.principal.hostname = $hostname
    // Exclude self-opens (process opening itself is benign)
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = $open.target.process.file.full_path
    // Exclude known-good cross-process openers (AV, EDR, debuggers)
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_suspended_process_parents

    // Enforce chronological ordering: suspended launch must precede the open
    $launch.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $open.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname, $parent_path over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(80)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1055.004")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($hostname)
    $injecting_process = array_distinct($parent_path)
    $target_processes_opened = array_distinct($open.target.process.file.full_path)
    $suspended_child_cmdlines = array_distinct($launch.target.process.command_line)

  condition:
    $launch and $open
}

rule MSSP_T1055_008_Ptrace_Injection_Proc_Mem_Access_Then_Suspicious_File {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects a non-debugger process opening /proc/<pid>/mem or /proc/<pid>/maps (indicative of ptrace-style memory manipulation) followed within 5 minutes by creation of a suspicious file in a world-writable or temporary location on the same host. This two-stage pattern is consistent with ptrace injection workflows that write a payload to disk before or after injecting into a target process."
    mitre_tactic    = "Defense Evasion, Privilege Escalation"
    mitre_technique = "T1055.008"
    mitre_technique_name = "Process Injection: Ptrace System Calls"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires Linux EDR or auditd file-access telemetry that records reads/opens of /proc/<pid>/mem and /proc/<pid>/maps, plus file-creation events. Auditd rules: -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S open,openat -F path=/proc -k ptrace_mem and -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S creat,open,openat -F dir=/tmp -k tmp_write."
    platform        = "Linux"
    log_source      = "linux_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Legitimate debuggers (gdb, lldb, strace, valgrind), Java JVM introspection agents, performance profilers (perf, async-profiler), container runtimes performing process inspection, and security agents that read /proc for monitoring purposes."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known debugger and profiler paths to %linux_allowed_proc_mem_readers. Add approved staging directories to %linux_allowed_staging_dirs. Narrow the file-creation filter to the specific world-writable paths most relevant to your environment."

  events:
    // Event 1: A non-privileged or unexpected process reads /proc/<pid>/mem or /proc/<pid>/maps
    // This is a strong indicator of ptrace-based memory inspection or injection preparation
    $open.metadata.event_type = "FILE_READ"
    $open.target.file.full_path = /\/proc\/[0-9]+\/(mem|maps|pagemap|syscall)$/ nocase
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path in %linux_allowed_proc_mem_readers
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\/(usr\/bin\/(gdb|strace|ltrace|valgrind)|usr\/lib\/jvm)/ nocase
    $open.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Adversaries commonly drop shellcode or shared objects to /tmp, /dev/shm, /var/tmp
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"
    $file.target.file.full_path = /^\/(tmp|dev\/shm|var\/tmp|run\/shm|proc\/[0-9]+\/fd)\// nocase
    not $file.target.file.full_path in %linux_allowed_staging_dirs
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\/(apt|dpkg|rpm|yum|dnf|snap|flatpak|pip|npm|cargo)/ nocase
    $file.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Chronological ordering: proc mem access must precede the suspicious file drop
    $open.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $file.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score          = max(80)
    $mitre_technique_id  = array_distinct("T1055.008")
    $primary_entity      = array_distinct($hostname)
    $proc_mem_paths      = array_distinct($open.target.file.full_path)
    $reading_process     = array_distinct($open.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $dropped_files       = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $writing_process     = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $affected_users      = array_distinct($open.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $open and $file
}

rule MSSP_T1055_009_ProcMem_Maps_Read_Then_Mem_Write {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects a two-stage /proc filesystem memory injection pattern: a process first reads the memory map of a target process via /proc/[pid]/maps (to enumerate gadgets and stack offsets), then within 5 minutes writes to /proc/[pid]/mem of the same target PID.     mitre_tactic    = "Defense Evasion, Privilege Escalation"
    mitre_technique = "T1055.009"
    mitre_technique_name = "Process Injection: Proc Memory"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires Linux EDR or auditd file-open/read/write telemetry normalised to Chronicle UDM FILE_READ and FILE_MODIFICATION events. Auditd rules must include -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S open,openat,read,write -F path=/proc for coverage."
    platform        = "Linux"
    log_source      = "linux_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Debuggers (gdb, lldb, strace), performance profilers (perf, valgrind), container runtimes performing introspection, and security agents that inspect process memory. Exclude known tooling paths via %linux_allowed_proc_readers."
    tuning_guidance = "Populate %linux_allowed_proc_readers with full paths of approved debuggers, profilers, and security agents (e.g. /usr/bin/gdb, /usr/bin/strace). Narrow further by adding a principal.user.userid exclusion list for privileged service accounts that legitimately inspect /proc."

    $read.metadata.event_type = "FILE_READ"
    $read.target.file.full_path = /\/proc\/[0-9]+\/maps$/ nocase
    not $read.principal.process.file.full_path in %linux_allowed_proc_readers
    $read.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Extract the numeric PID segment from the maps path for joining
    // We capture the directory portion /proc/<pid> as the join key
    $read.target.file.full_path = /\/proc\/(?P<pid>[0-9]+)\/maps$/

    $write.metadata.event_type = "FILE_MODIFICATION"
    $write.target.file.full_path = /\/proc\/[0-9]+\/mem$/ nocase
    not $write.principal.process.file.full_path in %linux_allowed_proc_readers
    $write.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Chronological ordering: maps read must precede mem write
    $read.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $write.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score        = max(85)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1055.009")
    $primary_entity    = array_distinct($hostname)
    $injecting_process = array_distinct($write.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $reading_process   = array_distinct($read.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $maps_paths_read   = array_distinct($read.target.file.full_path)
    $mem_paths_written = array_distinct($write.target.file.full_path)
    $actor_userid      = array_distinct($write.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $read and $write

rule MSSP_T1055_011_EWM_Injection_ProcessOpen_Then_Network {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects a suspicious process opening a handle to a remote process (PROCESS_OPEN) followed by an outbound network connection from the same process within 5 minutes.     mitre_tactic    = "Defense Evasion, Privilege Escalation"
    mitre_technique = "T1055.011"
    mitre_technique_name = "Process Injection: Extra Window Memory Injection"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR telemetry that emits PROCESS_OPEN events (cross-process handle acquisition) and NETWORK_CONNECTION events. CrowdStrike Falcon, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, and Sysmon (Event IDs 10 and 3) all produce this telemetry and are normalised into UDM by Chronicle."
    platform        = "Windows"
    log_source      = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Legitimate inter-process communication frameworks, debuggers (WinDbg, x64dbg), RMM agents that open handles to managed processes, AV/EDR self-protection modules, and software installers that inject into running processes for patching."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good parent process paths to %global_allowed_process_openers. Add trusted internal subnets to %rfc1918_internal to suppress internal-only connections. Narrow target.process.file.full_path patterns to exclude your RMM and AV binaries."

  events:
    // Leg 1: A non-system process opens a handle to a DIFFERENT process.
    // This is the prerequisite step for any cross-process injection technique,
    // including EWM injection (WriteProcessMemory + SetWindowLong pointer redirect).
    $open.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_OPEN"
    // Opener must not be a known Windows system binary
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\(csrss|lsass|services|svchost|wininit|winlogon|smss|System)\.exe$/ nocase
    // Opener must not be a known Windows system binary (use nocase correctly)
    $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\.exe$/ nocase

    $open.target.process.file.full_path = /\\(explorer|svchost|RuntimeBroker|SearchHost|ShellExperienceHost|sihost|taskhostw|dwm|ctfmon|dllhost)\.exe$/ nocase
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_process_openers
    $open.principal.hostname = $hostname
    $open.principal.process.pid = $injector_pid

    $net.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_CONNECTION"
    $net.principal.hostname = $hostname
    $net.principal.process.pid = $injector_pid
    // Exclude RFC-1918 to focus on external C2; internal-only can be tuned back in
    not $net.target.ip in %rfc1918_internal
    // Exclude common high-volume benign ports that are rarely C2
    not $net.target.port = 80
    not $net.target.port = 443
    not $net.target.port = 53

    $open.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $net.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname, $injector_pid over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score        = max(80)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1055.011")
    $primary_entity    = array_distinct($open.principal.hostname)
    $injector_process  = array_distinct($open.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $target_process    = array_distinct($open.target.process.file.full_path)
    $destination_ips   = array_distinct($net.target.ip)
    $destination_ports = array_distinct($net.target.port)

  condition:
    $open and $net
}

rule MSSP_T1055_013_Doppelganging_SuspParentSpawnsThenOpensMem {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "Critical"
    description     = "Detects a potential Process Doppelgänging sequence: a non-standard parent process launches a legitimate Windows host process (e.g. svchost, lsass, explorer) and within 5 minutes that same host opens a handle to another process with PROCESS_OPEN semantics.     mitre_tactic    = "Defense Evasion, Privilege Escalation"
    mitre_technique = "T1055.013"
    mitre_technique_name = "Process Injection: Process Doppelgänging"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR or Sysmon telemetry providing PROCESS_LAUNCH and PROCESS_OPEN events with process lineage and full image paths."
    platform        = "Windows"
    log_source      = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Security scanners, AV engines, and legitimate monitoring agents that open handles to system processes. Debuggers and profilers during development. Some RMM tools that inspect running processes."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good parent process paths to %global_allowed_doppel_parents. Add known-good opener paths to %global_allowed_process_openers. Narrow the host-process regex if svchost or explorer generate excessive noise in a specific environment."

  events:
    // Event 1: Suspicious parent spawns a legitimate Windows host process.
    // The parent is NOT one of the canonical launchers for these host binaries.
    $launch.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_LAUNCH"

    // Child must be a well-known host process that Doppelgänging typically targets.
    $launch.target.process.file.full_path = /\\(svchost|lsass|explorer|dllhost|taskhost|taskhostw|werfault|conhost|RuntimeBroker)\.exe$/ nocase

    not $launch.principal.process.file.full_path = /^[Cc]:\\[Ww][Ii][Nn][Dd][Oo][Ww][Ss]\\[Ss]ystem32\\/

    $launch.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Event 2: The newly spawned host process (or a process on the same host)

    $open.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_OPEN"

    // The opener should be the same host binary that was just spawned.
    $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\(svchost|lsass|explorer|dllhost|taskhost|taskhostw|werfault|conhost|RuntimeBroker)\.exe$/ nocase

    // Exclude openers that are known-good process inspection tools.
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_process_openers

    // Chronological ordering: launch must precede the process open.
    $launch.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $open.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score        = max(92)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1055.013")
    $primary_entity    = array_distinct($hostname)
    $spawned_process   = array_distinct($launch.target.process.file.full_path)
    $suspicious_parent = array_distinct($launch.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $opener_process    = array_distinct($open.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $target_opened_pid = array_distinct($open.target.process.pid)

  condition:
    $launch and $open
}

  outcome:

    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1055.014")
    $primary_entity    = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)

rule MSSP_T1055_014_VDSO_Hijack_Ptrace_Then_Anon_Mapping {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"

    $target_proc_paths   = array_distinct($open.target.file.full_path)

rule MSSP_T1055_015_ListPlanting_CrossProc_Handle_Then_Remote_Thread {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects the ListPlanting injection pattern: a non-system process opens a handle to a foreign process (PROCESS_OPEN) and, within 5 minutes, a new thread or child process is launched from that same victim process on the same host.     mitre_tactic    = "Defense Evasion, Privilege Escalation"
    mitre_technique = "T1055.015"
    mitre_technique_name = "Process Injection: ListPlanting"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR or Sysmon telemetry that emits PROCESS_OPEN events (Sysmon Event ID 10 / EDR equivalent) and PROCESS_LAUNCH events with parent process lineage. Both event types must be normalised into Chronicle UDM."
    platform        = "Windows"
    log_source      = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Legitimate automation frameworks (AutoHotkey, AutoIt), accessibility tools, screen-reader software, UI test harnesses (Selenium, WinAppDriver), and some RMM agents that enumerate or interact with GUI windows of other processes."

    // --- Leg 1: cross-process handle acquisition ---
    // A non-system, non-browser process opens a handle to a separate process.
    // This maps to Sysmon Event ID 10 / EDR PROCESS_OPEN telemetry.
    $open.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_OPEN"

    // Opener must not be a known-safe system binary
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\(lsass|csrss|smss|wininit|services|svchost|winlogon|dwm|taskhostw|sihost|fontdrvhost)\.exe$/ nocase
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\(MsMpEng|SenseIR|SenseCncProxy|MsSense)\.exe$/ nocase

    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_cross_proc_openers

    $child.target.process.file.full_path = /\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|certutil|bitsadmin|wmic|msiexec|installutil|cmstp|msbuild|regasm|regsvcs|ieexec|pcalua|forfiles|schtasks|at|net|nltest|whoami|ipconfig|systeminfo|tasklist|quser|query|sc|reg|wevtutil|vssadmin|bcdedit|cipher|expand|extrac32|hh|infdefaultinstall|makecab|mavinject|microsoft\.workflow\.compiler|msdeploy|msdt|msiexec|odbcconf|pcwrun|presentationhost|replace|rpcping|runscripthelper|syncappvpublishingserver|tttracer|xwizard)\.exe$/ nocase

  match:
    $hostname over 5m

  outcome:

    $mitre_technique_id  = array_distinct("T1055.015")
    $primary_entity      = array_distinct($hostname)
    $opener_process      = array_distinct($open.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $victim_process      = array_distinct($open.target.process.file.full_path)
    $spawned_child       = array_distinct($child.target.process.file.full_path)
    $child_command_line  = array_distinct($child.target.process.command_line)
    $opener_user         = array_distinct($open.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $open and $child
