rule MSSP_T1055_002_Process_Open_Then_Remote_Thread_Injection {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects a suspicious process opening a handle to a high-value Windows system process (PROCESS_OPEN) followed within 5 minutes by a remote thread or memory-write indicator surfacing as a PROCESS_INJECTION event on the same host. This sequence is characteristic of classic injection techniques such as VirtualAllocEx/WriteProcessMemory/CreateRemoteThread, QueueUserAPC injection, and reflective DLL injection. Deliberately avoids command-line matching to provide additive coverage over existing PROCESS_LAUNCH rules."
    mitre_tactic    = "Defense Evasion, Privilege Escalation"
    mitre_technique = "T1055"
    mitre_technique_name = "Process Injection"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR or Sysmon telemetry that emits PROCESS_OPEN (Sysmon Event ID 10) and PROCESS_INJECTION events normalised into Chronicle UDM. CrowdStrike Falcon, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, and SentinelOne all produce equivalent telemetry."
    platform        = "Windows"
    log_source      = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Legitimate debuggers (Visual Studio, WinDbg), AV/EDR self-protection threads, JIT compilers (JVM, CLR) opening sibling processes, RMM agents performing health checks against system processes."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good opener binaries (debuggers, RMM agents, JVM paths) to %global_allowed_injection_sources. Add authorised target process names to %global_allowed_injection_targets if a business application legitimately injects into them."

  events:
    // --- Leg 1: suspicious process opens a handle to a high-value system process ---
    $open.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_OPEN"

    // Opener must NOT be a known-good system binary opening itself
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_injection_sources

    // Target of the open handle is a canonical high-value Windows process
    $open.target.process.file.full_path = /\\(lsass|svchost|winlogon|csrss|explorer|spoolsv|services|wininit|dwm)\.exe$/ nocase

    // Opener is not itself one of those same canonical processes (avoids noisy self-opens)
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\(lsass|svchost|winlogon|csrss|wininit|services|dwm)\.exe$/ nocase

    $open.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // --- Leg 2: injection event on the same host within the window ---
    $inj.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_INJECTION"

    // The injecting process matches the opener from leg 1
    $inj.principal.process.file.full_path = $injector_path

    // Exclude known-good injection sources (same list)
    not $inj.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_injection_sources

    // Injection target is a high-value system process
    $inj.target.process.file.full_path = /\\(lsass|svchost|winlogon|csrss|explorer|spoolsv|services|wininit|dwm)\.exe$/ nocase

    $inj.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Anchor the opener to the same binary that later injects
    $open.principal.process.file.full_path = $injector_path

    // Chronological ordering: handle open precedes the injection event
    $open.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $inj.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname, $injector_path over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score          = max(85)
    $mitre_technique_id  = array_distinct("T1055")
    $primary_entity      = array_distinct($inj.principal.hostname)
    $injector_process    = array_distinct($inj.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $target_processes    = array_distinct($inj.target.process.file.full_path)
    $open_count          = count($open.metadata.id)
    $injection_count     = count($inj.metadata.id)

  condition:
    $open and $inj
}

rule MSSP_T1059_001_PowerShell_ScriptBlock_Artifact_Written {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Single-Event"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects PowerShell script-block logging writing suspicious script content to the Windows event log cache or AppData staging paths. PowerShell script-block logging (Event 4104) causes the engine to materialise decoded script content to disk before forwarding to the event log subsystem. Attackers who bypass command-line logging (e.g. via System.Management.Automation hosting, AMSI bypass, or reflective loading) still trigger this file-write artefact. The rule pivots on the FILE_CREATION / FILE_MODIFICATION layer rather than process command-line arguments, providing additive coverage orthogonal to PROCESS_LAUNCH rules."
    mitre_tactic    = "Execution"
    mitre_technique = "T1059.001"
    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR or Sysmon file-creation telemetry (Sysmon Event ID 11) with PowerShell script-block logging enabled (HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows\\PowerShell\\ScriptBlockLogging). EDR agents that surface FILE_CREATION events with the originating process path are sufficient."
    platform        = "Windows"
    log_source      = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Legitimate administrative PowerShell scripts, software deployment tools (SCCM, Intune), RMM agents, and security tooling that invoke PowerShell internally. Developers running complex build scripts may also trigger this."
    tuning_guidance = "Add trusted parent process paths (e.g. deployment agents, RMM binaries) to %global_allowed_ps_scriptblock_writers. Narrow the regex patterns if the environment generates high volume from known-good automation. Consider adding a minimum file-size threshold via EDR enrichment if available."

  events:
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"

    // Script-block logging cache files written by the PowerShell engine.
    // The engine writes decoded script content under the PSReadLine history
    // path, the Windows PowerShell transcript directory, or the script-block
    // ETW staging area. Match the originating process rather than a fixed path
    // so that renamed-binary and hosted-CLR scenarios are still caught.
    (
      $file.target.file.full_path = /\\Windows\\System32\\winevt\\Logs\\Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/ nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /\\AppData\\Roaming\\Microsoft\\Windows\\PowerShell\\PSReadLine\\/  nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /\\Transcripts\\.*\.txt$/ nocase
      or
      // Temporary script files written by the PowerShell engine before execution
      // (e.g. __PSScriptPolicyTest_*.ps1, tmp*.ps1 in TEMP)
      $file.target.file.full_path = /\\Temp\\.*\.ps1$/ nocase
      or
      $file.target.file.full_path = /\\Windows\\Temp\\.*\.ps1$/ nocase
    )

    // The writing process must be the PowerShell engine or a CLR host.
    // Matching on the DLL/assembly name catches reflective / hosted scenarios
    // where powershell.exe itself is not the process (e.g. PowerPick, Empire
    // stager injected into a non-PS process that loads SMA.dll).
    (
      $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\powershell\.exe$/ nocase
      or
      $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\pwsh\.exe$/ nocase
      or
      // Catch CLR-hosting processes that loaded System.Management.Automation
      $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\(wsmprovhost|wsmprovhost32|wsmprovhost64)\.exe$/ nocase
      or
      $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\(wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|msbuild|installutil)\.exe$/ nocase
    )

    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_ps_scriptblock_writers

  outcome:
    $risk_score        = max(72)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1059.001")
    $primary_entity    = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)
    $writing_process   = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $artifact_path     = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)

  condition:
    $file
}

rule MSSP_T1059_001_PowerShell_ScriptBlock_Then_FileWrite {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects a PowerShell process writing a suspicious file (script, executable, or archive) to disk shortly after script-block activity is observed on the same host. This targets the download-and-drop pattern without relying on command-line string matching, providing additive coverage beyond process-launch rules."
    mitre_tactic = "Execution"
    mitre_technique = "T1059.001"
    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR file-creation telemetry and PowerShell process-launch telemetry. PowerShell script-block logging (Event 4104) ingested via UDM is ideal but the rule also fires on any PowerShell process-launch followed by a file write."
    platform = "Windows"
    log_source = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Software deployment tools (SCCM, Chocolatey, Ansible), legitimate admin scripts that download and stage installers, patch management agents."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good parent process paths to %global_allowed_ps_parents and known-good destination directories to %global_allowed_ps_write_paths. Consider narrowing the file extension regex if archive drops are not relevant to the environment."

  events:
    // Event 1: PowerShell process launch (script-block or interactive session)
    $proc.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_LAUNCH"
    $proc.target.process.file.full_path = /\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/ nocase
    not $proc.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_ps_parents
    $proc.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Event 2: File creation by a PowerShell process on the same host
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"
    $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/ nocase
    // Suspicious extensions: scripts, executables, DLLs, archives, Office macros
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\.(ps1|psm1|psd1|bat|cmd|vbs|js|exe|dll|zip|7z|rar|cab|msi|hta|docm|xlsm|pptm)$/ nocase
    // Exclude common benign staging directories
    not $file.target.file.full_path = /\\(Windows\\Temp\\MpCmdRun|ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender)/ nocase
    not $file.target.file.full_path in %global_allowed_ps_write_paths
    $file.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Chronological ordering: process launch must precede the file write
    $proc.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $file.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(72)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1059.001")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($proc.principal.hostname)
    $ps_process_path = array_distinct($proc.target.process.file.full_path)
    $ps_parent_process = array_distinct($proc.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $files_written = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $file_write_count = count($file.target.file.full_path)

  condition:
    $proc and $file
}

rule MSSP_T1059_003_Batch_File_Drop_Suspicious_Location {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Single-Event"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects creation of batch files (.bat / .cmd) in locations commonly abused by adversaries: user temp directories, ProgramData, public user folders, and recycle bin paths. Attackers drop batch files as a staging artifact when leveraging the Windows command shell for execution. This rule targets the file-system state change rather than the process-creation event, providing coverage orthogonal to command-line detection."
    mitre_tactic    = "Execution"
    mitre_technique = "T1059.003"
    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR or Sysmon file-creation telemetry normalised to UDM FILE_CREATION events. Sysmon Event ID 11 or equivalent EDR file-write telemetry must be enabled."
    platform        = "Windows"
    log_source      = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Legitimate software installers that stage batch scripts in temp directories; RMM agents writing helper scripts to ProgramData; developer toolchains (npm, pip, build systems) that emit .bat wrappers."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good parent process paths (e.g. installer engines, RMM agents) to %global_allowed_batch_writers. Add approved staging directories to %global_allowed_batch_dirs if a specific product legitimately writes there."

  events:
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"

    // Target file must be a batch script by extension
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\.(bat|cmd)$/ nocase

    // Restrict to high-risk staging locations using regex with wildcard username
    // Covers: user temp, AppData, ProgramData, Public, Windows Temp, Recycle Bin
    $file.target.file.full_path = /(?i)(\\Users\\[^\\]+\\AppData\\(Local\\Temp|Roaming)|\\Users\\Public|\\ProgramData|\\Windows\\Temp|\\Temp\\|\\RECYCLER\\|\\\$Recycle\.Bin\\)/ nocase

    // Exclude known-good writers supplied via reference list
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_batch_writers

    // Exclude Windows system directories as the writing process origin
    // (e.g. msiexec writing to its own temp space is lower risk when parent is system)
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\Windows\\(System32|SysWOW64)\\msiexec\.exe$/ nocase

  outcome:
    $risk_score        = max(72)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1059.003")
    $primary_entity    = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)
    $dropped_file_path = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $writing_process   = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)

  condition:
    $file
}

rule MSSP_T1059_003_CmdShell_Drops_BatchFile_Then_Executes {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects a suspicious process writing a batch file (.bat or .cmd) to a user-writable or temp location, followed within 5 minutes by cmd.exe executing that same batch file. This two-stage pattern is additive coverage beyond simple cmd.exe command-line matching and targets adversaries who stage batch payloads before execution."
    mitre_tactic    = "Execution"
    mitre_technique = "T1059.003"
    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Script Interpreter: Windows Command Shell"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR or Sysmon file-creation telemetry (FILE_CREATION) and process-launch telemetry (PROCESS_LAUNCH) normalised into UDM. Both event types must be present for the correlation to fire."
    platform        = "Windows"
    log_source      = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Software installers that write and immediately run batch scripts, build systems (MSBuild, Ant, Maven), RMM agents deploying configuration scripts, legitimate IT automation frameworks."
    tuning_guidance = "Add trusted parent process paths to %global_allowed_batch_writers. Add known-good batch file directories to %global_allowed_batch_dirs. Narrow the file path regex if your environment writes batch files to specific approved locations."

  events:
    // Stage 1: A suspicious process writes a .bat or .cmd file to a
    // user-writable or temporary directory. We exclude known-good writers.
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\\(temp|tmp|appdata|public|programdata|users\\[^\\]+\\(downloads|desktop|documents))/ nocase
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\.(bat|cmd)$/ nocase
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_batch_writers
    not $file.target.file.full_path in %global_allowed_batch_dirs
    $file.principal.hostname = $hostname
    // Capture the written file path to join with the execution event
    $file.target.file.full_path = $batch_path

    // Stage 2: cmd.exe executes the same batch file within the time window.
    $proc.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_LAUNCH"
    $proc.target.process.file.full_path = /\\cmd\.exe$/ nocase
    // The command line references the batch file path written above
    $proc.target.process.command_line = /\.(bat|cmd)(\s|"|'|$)/ nocase
    // Exclude interactive cmd sessions launched from approved admin tools
    not $proc.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_batch_writers
    $proc.principal.hostname = $hostname
    $proc.target.process.command_line = $batch_path

    // Enforce chronological ordering: file must be written before execution
    $file.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $proc.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname, $batch_path over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score        = max(78)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1059.003")
    $primary_entity    = array_distinct($proc.principal.hostname)
    $batch_file_path   = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $writing_process   = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $executing_process = array_distinct($proc.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $cmd_commandline   = array_distinct($proc.target.process.command_line)

  condition:
    $file and $proc
}

rule MSSP_T1059_004_ESXi_Shell_Script_File_Creation {

    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires ESXi file activity telemetry normalised to UDM FILE_CREATION events. Typically sourced from hostd or an EDR agent deployed on ESXi (e.g. Carbon Black, VMware Contexa). Confirm FILE_CREATION events are ingested from the vmware_esxi log source."

    // Exclude authorised script-writing processes across MSSP client environments
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %esxi_allowed_script_writers

    not $file.target.file.full_path in %esxi_allowed_datastore_paths

rule MSSP_T1059_004_Shell_Script_Drop_Then_Outbound_Connection {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects a shell script written to a world-writable or temporary Linux path followed within 5 minutes by an outbound network connection from the same host. This pattern is consistent with a Unix shell payload being staged and then beaconing out or downloading secondary tooling. Complements existing process-launch/command-line detections by using firewall-observable network behaviour correlated with endpoint file-creation telemetry."
    mitre_tactic = "Execution"
    mitre_technique = "T1059.004"
    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires Linux EDR or auditd FILE_CREATION telemetry AND firewall/perimeter NETWORK_CONNECTION or NETWORK_FLOW logs. Both sources must populate principal.hostname with the same normalised value."
    platform = "Linux"
    log_source = "firewall"
    false_positives = "Legitimate software installers writing scripts to /tmp then phoning home for updates; configuration management agents (Ansible, Chef, Puppet); container orchestration health checks; developer workstations running build pipelines."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good source hosts to %linux_allowed_script_hosts. Add approved external CIDRs or destinations to %linux_allowed_update_destinations. Narrow the file path regex if /tmp activity is too noisy in your environment."

  events:
    // Leg 1: shell script file created in a world-writable or staging path on Linux
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"
    $file.target.file.full_path = /^(\/tmp\/|\/var\/tmp\/|\/dev\/shm\/|\/run\/|\/var\/run\/)/ nocase
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\.(sh|bash|ksh|zsh|ash|csh|tcsh|py|pl|rb)$/ nocase
    not $file.principal.hostname in %linux_allowed_script_hosts
    $file.principal.hostname = $src_host

    $net.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_CONNECTION"
    not $net.target.ip in %linux_allowed_update_destinations
    not $net.target.ip in %rfc1918_internal
    $net.target.port > 0
    $net.principal.hostname = $src_host

    // Enforce chronological ordering: file drop happens before the outbound connection
    $file.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $net.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $src_host over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(78)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1059.004")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($src_host)
    $dropped_script_paths = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $destination_ips = array_distinct($net.target.ip)
    $destination_ports = array_distinct($net.target.port)
    $connection_count = count($net.target.ip)

  condition:
    $file and $net
}

rule MSSP_T1059_005_VBScript_File_Write_Then_Exec_Linux {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects a VBScript or VBA-related file written to a world-writable or temporary directory on Linux, followed within 5 minutes by a process launch that executes or interprets that same file.     mitre_tactic    = "Execution"
    mitre_technique = "T1059.005"
    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires Linux EDR or auditd telemetry normalised to Chronicle UDM, producing FILE_CREATION and PROCESS_LAUNCH events with principal.hostname, target.file.full_path, and target.process.command_line populated."
    platform        = "Linux"
    log_source      = "linux_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Legitimate .NET or Mono development workflows writing and running VB scripts in /tmp; CI/CD pipelines; automated test harnesses using Mono VB compiler."
    tuning_guidance = "Add trusted parent process paths to %linux_allowed_vb_interpreters and trusted staging directories to %linux_allowed_vb_staging_dirs. Consider scoping by principal.user.userid to exclude known build service accounts."

  events:
    // Event 1: A .vb, .vbs, or .vba file is written into a world-writable or
    // staging directory. Pre-filtered to suspicious paths only to avoid
    // joining against every file write on the host.
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"
    $file.target.file.full_path = /^(\/tmp\/|\/var\/tmp\/|\/dev\/shm\/|\/run\/|\/var\/run\/)/ nocase
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\.(vb|vbs|vba)$/ nocase
    not $file.target.file.full_path in %linux_allowed_vb_staging_dirs
    $file.principal.hostname = $hostname

    log_prerequisites    = "Requires Linux EDR or auditd file-write telemetry normalised to Chronicle UDM FILE_CREATION or FILE_MODIFICATION events with target.file.full_path populated."
    platform             = "Linux"
    log_source           = "linux_endpoint"
    false_positives      = "Package managers (pip, apt, yum) writing compiled .pyc files to /tmp during install; CI/CD pipelines staging build artefacts; legitimate automation frameworks using /tmp for ephemeral scripts."

rule MSSP_T1059_007_JS_Script_File_Drop_Artifact {

    platform = "Windows"
    log_source = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Web developers writing .js files under project directories, legitimate software installers dropping .hta setup wizards, enterprise RMM agents deploying .wsf configuration scripts, Node.js package managers."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good parent process paths (e.g. software installers, IDE processes) to %global_allowed_script_drop_parents.   events:

    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_script_drop_parents

rule MSSP_T1059_007_JS_Runtime_Drops_File_To_Writable_Dir {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects a JavaScript runtime process (node, deno, bun) that launches and subsequently creates or modifies a file in a world-writable or staging directory (/tmp, /dev/shm, /var/tmp).     mitre_tactic    = "Execution"
    mitre_technique = "T1059.007"
    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires Linux EDR or auditd telemetry normalised to Chronicle UDM, producing PROCESS_LAUNCH and FILE_CREATION or FILE_MODIFICATION events with principal.process lineage and target.file.full_path populated."
    platform        = "Linux"
    log_source      = "linux_endpoint"
    false_positives = "CI/CD pipelines running npm build steps that emit artifacts to /tmp; containerised test runners; legitimate Node.js server applications writing to /tmp for IPC sockets; package managers (npm, yarn) extracting to temp directories."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known CI/CD runner hostnames to %linux_allowed_js_runtime_hosts. Add approved parent process paths (e.g. Jenkins agent, GitLab runner) to %linux_allowed_js_parent_procs. Narrow the file path regex if only specific subdirectories are abused in your environment."

  events:

    $proc.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_LAUNCH"
    $proc.target.process.file.full_path = /\/(node|nodejs|deno|bun)$/ nocase
    not $proc.principal.process.file.full_path in %linux_allowed_js_parent_procs
    not $proc.principal.hostname in %linux_allowed_js_runtime_hosts

    $proc.target.process.pid = $js_pid

    $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\/(node|nodejs|deno|bun)$/ nocase
    $file.principal.hostname = $hostname
    $file.principal.process.pid = $js_pid

    $proc.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $file.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

    $parent_process      = array_distinct($proc.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $staged_files        = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $js_cmdline          = array_distinct($proc.target.process.command_line)

rule MSSP_T1059_008_Network_Device_CLI_Remote_Mgmt_Connection {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects inbound network connections to management-plane ports (SSH, Telnet, NETCONF, REST API) on network devices originating from addresses outside known internal management ranges. Adversaries abusing T1059.008 must first establish CLI access remotely; this rule catches the network-observable session establishment from unexpected source space, which is additive to any process/command-line coverage."
    mitre_tactic = "Execution"
    mitre_technique = "T1059.008"
    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Scripting Interpreter: Network Device CLI"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires firewall or perimeter flow/connection logs that record inbound sessions to network device management addresses. Flow records must include source IP, destination IP, and destination port."
    platform = "Network Devices"
    log_source = "firewall"
    false_positives = "Authorized network engineers connecting from jump hosts or VPN egress IPs not yet added to the allowlist; automated monitoring systems (SNMP pollers, NMS platforms) using SSH; CI/CD pipeline automation for network configuration management."
    tuning_guidance = "Populate %mgmt_allowed_source_ips with all approved jump-host, VPN egress, and NMS source addresses. Populate %mgmt_device_ips with the management-plane IP addresses of all monitored network devices. Reduce severity to Medium once allowlists are mature. Consider adding a threshold wrapper if alert volume is high."

  events:
    $net.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_CONNECTION"

    // Target must be a known network device management address
    $net.target.ip in %mgmt_device_ips

    // Management-plane ports: SSH (22), Telnet (23), NETCONF-SSH (830),
    // NETCONF-BEEP (831), RESTCONF (443 handled separately), gRPC (57400),
    // legacy device HTTP management (80), HTTPS management (443)
    // Narrow to the highest-signal unencrypted and dedicated mgmt ports
    (
      $net.target.port = 22   or
      $net.target.port = 23   or
      $net.target.port = 830  or
      $net.target.port = 831  or
      $net.target.port = 57400
    )

    // Source must NOT be an approved management source
    not $net.principal.ip in %mgmt_allowed_source_ips

    // Source must NOT be internal RFC-1918 / management network space
    // (belt-and-suspenders: allowlist is primary control, this catches
    //  any internal ranges not yet enumerated in the allowlist)
    not $net.principal.ip in %rfc1918_internal

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(75)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1059.008")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($net.target.ip)
    $source_ip = array_distinct($net.principal.ip)
    $destination_port = array_distinct($net.target.port)

  condition:
    $net
}

    log_source      = "identity"

rule MSSP_T1059_010_AutoHotKey_AutoIT_Script_File_Creation {

    description = "Detects creation of AutoHotKey (.ahk) or AutoIT (.au3) script files on disk. This rule pivots on the file artifact produced rather than the process command line, providing coverage that is harder to evade than process-creation logging alone."

    mitre_technique = "T1059.010"
    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Scripting Interpreter: AutoHotKey & AutoIT"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR or Sysmon file-creation telemetry normalised to UDM FILE_CREATION events. Sysmon Event ID 11 or equivalent EDR file-write telemetry must be enabled."
    platform = "Windows"
    log_source = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Legitimate automation engineers writing AHK or AutoIT scripts for UI testing, RPA workflows, or IT helpdesk tooling. Software installers that unpack AutoIT-compiled bundles to a temp directory."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good parent process paths (e.g., IDE executables, RPA platform agents) to %global_allowed_autoit_ahk_parents.     not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_autoit_ahk_parents

    not $file.target.file.full_path in %global_allowed_script_drop_paths

  outcome:

    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1059.010")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)
    $dropped_script_path = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $writing_process = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)

}

rule MSSP_T1059_010_AutoScript_Drops_File_Then_Network {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects an AutoIT or AutoHotKey interpreter spawning a child process that subsequently creates a file in a user-writable or temp directory, indicating potential payload staging or dropper activity. This provides additive coverage beyond command-line detection by correlating process lineage with file-write behaviour."
    mitre_tactic = "Execution"
    mitre_technique = "T1059.010"
    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Scripting Interpreter: AutoHotKey & AutoIT"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR process telemetry (PROCESS_LAUNCH) and file telemetry (FILE_CREATION) normalised into UDM. Both event types must be present for the correlation to fire."
    platform = "Windows"
    log_source = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Legitimate AutoIT-packaged installers, AutoHotKey productivity macros that write config or log files, software deployment tools bundled with AutoIT runtimes."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good AutoIT/AHK parent process full paths to %autoscript_allowed_parents. Add approved child process paths to %autoscript_allowed_children. Add sanctioned write directories to %autoscript_allowed_write_dirs."

  events:
    // Event 1: AutoIT or AutoHotKey interpreter (or compiled equivalent) launches a child process
    $proc.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_LAUNCH"
    (
      $proc.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\(AutoIt3|AutoIt3_x64|AutoHotkey|AutoHotkeyU32|AutoHotkeyU64|AutoHotkeyA32)\.exe$/ nocase
      or
      $proc.principal.process.command_line = /\.(au3|ahk)(\s|"|'|$)/ nocase
    )
    not $proc.principal.process.file.full_path in %autoscript_allowed_parents
    not $proc.target.process.file.full_path in %autoscript_allowed_children
    $proc.principal.hostname = $hostname
    $proc.target.process.pid = $child_pid

    // Event 2: That same child process creates a file in a suspicious writable location
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"
    $file.principal.hostname = $hostname
    $file.principal.process.pid = $child_pid
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\\(Temp|AppData|ProgramData|Users\\[^\\]+\\(Downloads|Desktop|Documents|AppData))\\/ nocase
    not $file.target.file.full_path in %autoscript_allowed_write_dirs

    // Chronological ordering: process launch must precede file creation
    $proc.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $file.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname, $child_pid over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(80)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1059.010")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($proc.principal.hostname)
    $autoscript_parent = array_distinct($proc.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $child_process = array_distinct($proc.target.process.file.full_path)
    $child_cmdline = array_distinct($proc.target.process.command_line)
    $files_created = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $event_count = count($file.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds)

  condition:
    $proc and $file
}

rule MSSP_T1059_011_Lua_Network_Outbound_Connection {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "Medium"
    description = "Detects outbound network connections to non-internal destinations on ports commonly used by Lua-based implants and malware (e.g., PoetRat, EvilBunny, Sunseed). Lua interpreters embedded in malware frequently beacon to C2 infrastructure over standard or high-numbered ports. This rule pivots to the network perimeter to provide additive coverage beyond process-launch detections."
    mitre_tactic = "Execution"
    mitre_technique = "T1059.011"
    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Scripting Interpreter: Lua"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires firewall or perimeter flow logs normalised to Chronicle UDM NETWORK_CONNECTION or NETWORK_FLOW. Source IP must be a Windows host on the internal network."
    platform = "Windows"
    log_source = "firewall"
    false_positives = "Legitimate applications embedding Lua (e.g., game engines, network monitoring tools, Wireshark with Lua plugins, Nmap scripting engine) making outbound connections. Software update mechanisms for Lua-embedded products."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good internal source IPs or subnets to %lua_network_allowed_sources. Add approved external destination CIDRs or IPs to %lua_network_allowed_destinations. Narrow the port list if your environment uses a strict egress policy. Consider raising severity if combined with a concurrent process-launch alert for lua.exe or luac.exe."

  events:
    $net.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_CONNECTION"

    // Outbound connection: source is internal, destination is external
    $net.principal.ip in %internal_corporate_subnets
    not $net.target.ip in %internal_corporate_subnets
    not $net.target.ip in %lua_network_allowed_destinations

    // Exclude known-good source hosts (e.g., approved Lua-embedding application servers)
    not $net.principal.ip in %lua_network_allowed_sources

    // Target ports associated with Lua-based C2 implant activity:
    // 80/443 covered by proxy rules; focus on non-standard ports seen in
    // PoetRat (8080, 8443), EvilBunny (high ephemeral C2), and generic
    // reverse-shell patterns over uncommon ports.
    // Match high-numbered non-ephemeral ports (1024-49151) excluding
    // well-known service ports that have dedicated detections.
    (
      $net.target.port = 4444 or
      $net.target.port = 4445 or
      $net.target.port = 8080 or
      $net.target.port = 8443 or
      $net.target.port = 8888 or
      $net.target.port = 9090 or
      $net.target.port = 9999 or
      $net.target.port = 1337 or
      $net.target.port = 31337 or
      $net.target.port = 6666 or
      $net.target.port = 7777 or
      $net.target.port = 2222 or
      $net.target.port = 3333
    )

    // Connection must be TCP (Lua C2 implants use TCP streams)
    $net.network.ip_protocol = "TCP"

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(60)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1059.011")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($net.principal.ip)
    $destination_ip = array_distinct($net.target.ip)
    $destination_port = array_distinct($net.target.port)

  condition:
    $net
}

rule MSSP_T1059_011_Lua_Script_Drop_Then_Outbound_Connection {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects a Lua script file written to a world-writable or temporary Linux path followed within 5 minutes by an outbound network connection from the same host. This pattern is consistent with adversaries staging and executing Lua payloads that beacon or exfiltrate data. Variant 2 of 2 for T1059.011 - network-observable coverage via firewall telemetry correlated with endpoint file-creation events."
    mitre_tactic = "Execution"
    mitre_technique = "T1059.011"
    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Scripting Interpreter: Lua"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires Linux EDR or auditd FILE_CREATION telemetry AND firewall/perimeter NETWORK_CONNECTION or NETWORK_FLOW logs normalised into Chronicle UDM. Both log sources must populate principal.hostname consistently for the join to succeed."
    platform = "Linux"
    log_source = "firewall"
    false_positives = "Legitimate software installers that write Lua configuration files (e.g., Neovim plugins, OpenResty deployments, game engines). Monitoring agents that write Lua scripts to /tmp for health checks. CI/CD pipelines running Lua-based build tools."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good source hosts to %lua_script_drop_allowed_hosts. Add approved external destinations to %lua_outbound_allowed_destinations. Narrow the file path regex if your environment uses a specific staging directory. Raise risk_score if the destination port is non-standard (not 80/443)."

  events:
    // Leg 1: A Lua script file is created in a suspicious Linux path
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\/(tmp|var\/tmp|dev\/shm|run\/shm|var\/run|home\/[^\/]+\/(\.cache|\.config|\.local)|opt\/[^\/]+)\/[^\/]+\.lua$/ nocase
    not $file.principal.hostname in %lua_script_drop_allowed_hosts
    $file.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Leg 2: An outbound network connection from the same host shortly after
    $net.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_CONNECTION"
    $net.principal.hostname = $hostname
    not $net.target.ip in %lua_outbound_allowed_destinations
    not $net.target.ip in %rfc1918_internal
    // Exclude loopback and link-local ranges via reference list; also exclude DNS-only port 53 noise
    $net.target.port != 53

    // Chronological ordering: file drop must precede the outbound connection
    $file.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $net.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(72)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1059.011")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($hostname)
    $dropped_lua_paths = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $outbound_destination_ips = array_distinct($net.target.ip)
    $outbound_destination_ports = array_distinct($net.target.port)
    $connection_count = count($net.target.ip)

  condition:
    $file and $net
}

rule MSSP_T1059_012_ESXi_Firewall_Config_Modified {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects modification of ESXi host firewall or network configuration files that result from hypervisor CLI abuse (esxcli, vim-cmd). Adversaries use these CLIs to open firewall rules, redirect syslog, or alter host networking to support C2 or data exfiltration. This rule pivots on the resulting file artifact rather than the command line, providing coverage when process-creation telemetry is suppressed or tampered with."
    mitre_tactic = "Execution"
    mitre_technique = "T1059.012"
    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Scripting Interpreter: Hypervisor CLI"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires ESXi file-activity telemetry from hostd or a host-based agent capable of emitting FILE_MODIFICATION/FILE_CREATION UDM events for /etc/vmware paths. VMware Carbon Black, Sysdig Falco on ESXi, or equivalent host sensor required."
    platform = "ESXi"
    log_source = "vmware_esxi"
    false_positives = "Authorised vSphere administrators applying firewall policy changes via vCenter, automated configuration management (Ansible, Puppet) targeting ESXi hosts, VMware Update Manager applying patches that touch /etc/vmware."
    tuning_guidance = "Populate %esxi_allowed_config_writers with the full paths of authorised management agents (e.g. /usr/lib/vmware/vpxa/bin/vpxa). Add known-good parent process paths for automated patching workflows. Narrow scope further by restricting to after-hours windows using a scheduled suppression list."

  events:
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_MODIFICATION"

    // Target ESXi host configuration paths written by hypervisor CLI activity.
    // Covers firewall ruleset XML, syslog config, network config, and the
    // authorised-keys file (a common persistence artefact from CLI abuse).
    $file.target.file.full_path = /^\/(etc\/vmware\/(firewall|esx\.conf|syslog\.conf|rhttpproxy|vmkiscsid|pam\.d)|etc\/ssh\/keys-root\/authorized_keys|scratch\/log|vmfs\/volumes\/[^\/]+\/\.locker)/ nocase

    // Optionally correlate the writing process when the sensor populates it.
    // Matches esxcli, vim-cmd, esxcfg-*, localcli, and similar hypervisor CLIs
    // without hardcoding a single binary name.
    (
      $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\/(esxcli|vim-cmd|esxcfg-|localcli|esxconfig|hostd-probe|busybox)/ nocase
      or
      $file.principal.process.file.full_path = ""  // allow events where process field is unpopulated
    )

    // Exclude known-good authorised management agents via reference list.
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %esxi_allowed_config_writers

    // Exclude the ESXi config paths that are written at every normal boot
    // to avoid flooding on host restarts.
    not $file.target.file.full_path = /\/etc\/vmware\/esx\.conf\.bak/ nocase

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(78)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1059.012")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)
    $modified_path = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $writing_process = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)

  condition:
    $file
}

rule MSSP_T1059_012_ESXi_Login_Then_VM_Manipulation {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects an interactive login to an ESXi host followed within 5 minutes by a setting modification or VM management action on the same host. This sequence is consistent with adversaries authenticating to the hypervisor management plane and then abusing esxcli, vim-cmd, or similar CLIs to manipulate virtual machines or host configuration. Variant 2 of 2 for T1059.012 - focuses on the login-to-action sequence rather than command-line content."
    mitre_tactic = "Execution"
    mitre_technique = "T1059.012"
    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Scripting Interpreter: Hypervisor CLI"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires ESXi hostd and shell telemetry forwarded to Chronicle via syslog or the VMware ESXi log source. USER_LOGIN events from hostd authentication and SETTING_MODIFICATION events from hostd/vim-cmd activity must both be ingested."
    platform = "ESXi"
    log_source = "vmware_esxi"
    false_positives = "Authorized VMware administrators performing routine maintenance, automated orchestration systems (vCenter, Ansible, Terraform) authenticating and reconfiguring hosts, backup agents interacting with the management plane."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known administrative service accounts to %esxi_allowed_admin_accounts. Add known orchestration hostnames or IPs to %esxi_allowed_mgmt_sources. Narrow the time window if the environment has high-frequency automated management activity."

  events:
    // Leg 1: Interactive or remote login to the ESXi management plane
    $auth.metadata.event_type = "USER_LOGIN"
    $auth.principal.hostname = $esxi_host
    $auth.target.user.userid != ""
    not $auth.target.user.userid in %esxi_allowed_admin_accounts
    not $auth.principal.ip in %esxi_allowed_mgmt_sources

    // Leg 2: Host or VM configuration change following the login on the same host
    $cfg.metadata.event_type = "SETTING_MODIFICATION"
    $cfg.principal.hostname = $esxi_host
    $cfg.target.user.userid != ""

    // Chronological ordering: login must precede the configuration change
    $auth.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $cfg.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $esxi_host over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(72)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1059.012")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($esxi_host)
    $authenticated_user = array_distinct($auth.target.user.userid)
    $modifying_user = array_distinct($cfg.target.user.userid)
    $login_source_ip = array_distinct($auth.principal.ip)
    $modified_setting = array_distinct($cfg.target.resource.name)
    $event_count = count($cfg.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds)

  condition:
    $auth and $cfg
}

rule MSSP_T1059_013_Container_API_Exec_Resource_Access {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Engineering"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects container exec/attach API calls recorded in cloud audit logs. These calls represent the state-change artifact of an adversary using the container CLI or API to execute commands inside a running container (T1059.013). This rule targets the audit-log layer rather than process command-line telemetry, providing additive coverage that is harder to evade."
    mitre_tactic = "Execution"
    mitre_technique = "T1059.013"
    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Scripting Interpreter: Container CLI/API"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires cloud provider audit logs (e.g., GCP Audit Logs, AWS CloudTrail, Azure Activity Logs) normalised into Chronicle UDM. Container exec/attach API calls must be captured. For Kubernetes, enable audit policy at Request/Response level for the 'pods/exec' and 'pods/attach' sub-resources."
    platform = "Containers"
    log_source = "cloud_audit"
    false_positives = "Legitimate DevOps engineers running ad-hoc debug sessions, CI/CD pipeline health checks that exec into containers, monitoring agents that attach to containers for metrics collection."
    tuning_guidance = "Populate %container_exec_allowed_principals with approved service accounts and human users who routinely exec into containers (e.g., CI/CD service accounts, on-call SRE accounts). Populate %container_exec_allowed_namespaces with low-risk namespaces such as dedicated debug or tooling namespaces. Raise severity or alert immediately when the principal is anonymous or a default service account."

  events:
    $cloud.metadata.event_type = "USER_RESOURCE_ACCESS"

    // Match exec, attach, or run API sub-resource patterns normalised into the method/operation field.
    // Covers Kubernetes pods/exec, pods/attach, and equivalent container runtime API verbs.
    $cloud.target.resource.name = /\/(exec|attach|run)(\?|$|\/)/ nocase

    // Restrict to container or pod resource types to avoid matching unrelated exec-style calls.
    $cloud.target.resource.resource_type = /(pod|container)/ nocase

    // Exclude approved principals performing routine exec operations.
    not $cloud.principal.user.userid in %container_exec_allowed_principals

    // Exclude approved namespaces where exec is expected and controlled.
    not $cloud.target.resource.attribute.labels["namespace"] in %container_exec_allowed_namespaces

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(75)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1059.013")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($cloud.principal.user.userid)
    $target_resource = array_distinct($cloud.target.resource.name)
    $resource_type = array_distinct($cloud.target.resource.resource_type)
    $caller_ip = array_distinct($cloud.principal.ip)

  condition:
    $cloud
}

rule MSSP_T1059_013_Container_API_Exec_Then_Sensitive_Resource_Access {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects a cloud audit event for an interactive exec/attach session into a running container followed by a sensitive resource access (secrets, credentials, config maps) within the same time window. This pattern indicates adversarial use of the container CLI/API to execute commands and then harvest sensitive data from the control plane, without relying on process-level command-line telemetry."
    mitre_tactic = "Execution"
    mitre_technique = "T1059.013"
    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Scripting Interpreter: Container CLI/API"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires cloud provider audit logs (e.g. Kubernetes API server audit, GCP Audit, Azure Activity, CloudTrail) normalised into Chronicle UDM. The exec/attach verb must be captured as USER_RESOURCE_ACCESS and secret/configmap reads as USER_RESOURCE_ACCESS or RESOURCE_CREATION events."
    platform = "Containers"
    log_source = "cloud_audit"
    false_positives = "Legitimate DevOps engineers exec-ing into pods for debugging; CI/CD pipelines that mount secrets and exec health checks; operator tooling that reads config maps during reconciliation loops."
    tuning_guidance = "Populate %container_allowed_exec_principals with approved service accounts and human users permitted to exec into pods. Populate %container_allowed_secret_readers with automation identities that legitimately read secrets immediately after exec events. Narrow the resource_type filter if your environment uses custom secret backends."

  events:
    // Event 1: Interactive exec or attach into a running container via the API
    $exec.metadata.event_type = "USER_RESOURCE_ACCESS"
    $exec.target.resource.resource_type = "CONTAINER"
    // Match exec, attach, or portforward verbs normalised into the resource name or operation
    (
      $exec.target.resource.name = /\/exec$/ nocase or
      $exec.target.resource.name = /\/attach$/ nocase or
      $exec.target.resource.name = /\/portforward$/ nocase or
      $exec.metadata.product_event_type = /exec/ nocase or
      $exec.metadata.product_event_type = /attach/ nocase
    )
    not $exec.principal.user.userid in %container_allowed_exec_principals
    // Join anchor: the principal identity performing both actions
    $exec.principal.user.userid = $actor

    // Event 2: Sensitive resource read (secrets, credentials, config maps) shortly after
    $secret.metadata.event_type = "USER_RESOURCE_ACCESS"
    (
      $secret.target.resource.resource_type = "CREDENTIAL" or
      $secret.target.resource.name = /secret/ nocase or
      $secret.target.resource.name = /configmap/ nocase or
      $secret.target.resource.name = /serviceaccount.*token/ nocase or
      $secret.target.resource.name = /credential/ nocase
    )
    not $secret.principal.user.userid in %container_allowed_secret_readers
    $secret.principal.user.userid = $actor

    // Chronological ordering: exec must precede the sensitive read
    $exec.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $secret.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $actor over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(80)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1059.013")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($actor)
    $exec_targets = array_distinct($exec.target.resource.name)
    $secret_targets = array_distinct($secret.target.resource.name)
    $source_ips = array_distinct($exec.principal.ip)
    $event_count = count($secret.metadata.id)

  condition:
    $exec and $secret
}

rule MSSP_T1059_Office_Suite_Script_Execution_Via_Macro_Setting_Change {

    description = "Detects modification of macro or script execution settings within an Office Suite tenant (Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace).     mitre_tactic = "Execution"
    mitre_technique = "T1059"
    mitre_technique_name = "Command and Scripting Interpreter"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires Microsoft 365 Unified Audit Log (UAL) or Google Workspace Admin Audit logs forwarded to Chronicle. Key operations: Set-OrgConfig, Set-UserConfig, UpdatedSettings, AdminSettingsChanged, or equivalent policy change events normalised to SETTING_MODIFICATION in UDM."
    platform = "Office Suite"
    log_source = "vmware_esxi"

    $cfg.metadata.event_type = "SETTING_MODIFICATION"

    not $cfg.principal.hostname in %esxi_approved_automation_hosts

    $auth.metadata.event_type = "USER_LOGIN"
    $auth.target.hostname = $esxi_host
    not $auth.principal.user.userid in %esxi_approved_shell_enablement_accounts

    $cfg.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $auth.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

    $mitre_technique_id  = array_distinct("T1059")

    $authenticating_user = array_distinct($auth.principal.user.userid)

    $login_count         = count($auth.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds)

rule MSSP_T1071_001_Linux_Beaconing_Then_Anomalous_HTTP_Sequence {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects a Linux host exhibiting high-frequency outbound HTTP/S connections to a single external destination followed by a large HTTP response, consistent with C2 beaconing over web protocols. The first event captures repetitive short-interval connections (beacon cadence) and the second captures an anomalously large inbound transfer on the same host/destination pair, suggesting tool staging or data exfiltration wrapped in HTTP."
    mitre_tactic = "Command and Control"
    mitre_technique = "T1071.001"
    mitre_technique_name = "Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires firewall or perimeter proxy logs normalised to Chronicle UDM NETWORK_FLOW and NETWORK_HTTP events. Flow records must include bytes_sent/bytes_received (network.sent_bytes / network.received_bytes). HTTP records must include response content-length or body size."
    platform = "Linux"
    log_source = "firewall"
    false_positives = "Software update clients (apt, yum, snap) polling CDNs; monitoring agents with frequent heartbeats; streaming media clients; legitimate large file downloads from cloud storage."
    tuning_guidance = "Populate %firewall_allowed_external_destinations with approved CDN and update server ranges. Populate %firewall_internal_address_space with all RFC-1918 and site-local ranges. Raise the received_bytes threshold if large legitimate downloads are common. Narrow the beacon window by reducing the time window or increasing the minimum connection count threshold."

  events:
    // Leg 1: High-frequency outbound NETWORK_FLOW from an internal Linux host
    // to a single external destination - beacon cadence signal.
    // Pre-filter: only flows on HTTP/S ports to non-internal destinations.
    $flow.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_FLOW"
    $flow.target.port = 80 or
    $flow.target.port = 443 or
    $flow.target.port = 8080 or
    $flow.target.port = 8443
    not $flow.target.ip in %firewall_internal_address_space
    not $flow.target.ip in %firewall_allowed_external_destinations
    // Bind join placeholders: source host and destination IP must match leg 2.
    $flow.principal.ip = $src_ip
    $flow.target.ip = $dst_ip

    // Leg 2: Anomalously large HTTP response from the same external destination
    // back to the same internal host - staging payload or C2 response.
    // Pre-filter: only HTTP events with large inbound body.
    $http.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_HTTP"
    $http.network.received_bytes > 500000
    not $http.target.ip in %firewall_internal_address_space
    not $http.target.ip in %firewall_allowed_external_destinations
    // Bind same join placeholders.
    $http.principal.ip = $src_ip
    $http.target.ip = $dst_ip

    // Chronological ordering: beacon flows observed before the large response.
    $flow.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $http.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $src_ip, $dst_ip over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(78)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1071.001")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($src_ip)
    $destination_ip = array_distinct($dst_ip)
    $destination_ports = array_distinct($flow.target.port)
    $total_flows = count($flow.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds)
    $max_response_bytes = max($http.network.received_bytes)
    $http_methods_observed = array_distinct($http.network.http.method)

  condition:
    $flow and $http
}

rule MSSP_T1071_002_FileTransferProtocol_Outbound_Network {

    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Single-Event"
    severity        = "Medium"
    description     = "Detects outbound connections on file-transfer protocol ports (FTP 21, FTPS 990, TFTP 69, SMB 445, FTP-data 20) from internal hosts to external destinations. Adversaries abuse these protocols for C2 traffic that blends with legitimate file-transfer activity. Firewall/perimeter telemetry only - no process context required."
    mitre_tactic    = "Command and Control"
    mitre_technique = "T1071.002"
    mitre_technique_name = "Application Layer Protocol: File Transfer Protocols"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires firewall or perimeter flow/connection logs normalised into Chronicle UDM NETWORK_CONNECTION or NETWORK_FLOW events. Source IP must be populated and destination IP must be external."
    platform        = "Linux"
    log_source      = "firewall"
    false_positives = "Legitimate FTP/SFTP backup jobs to external storage providers, software update mirrors using FTP, managed file-transfer appliances, TFTP for network device provisioning, SMB to cloud file-share gateways."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good external FTP/FTPS/TFTP/SMB destinations to %global_allowed_filetransfer_destinations.   events:

    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1071.002")
    $primary_entity    = array_distinct($net.principal.ip)

    $destination_ports = array_distinct($net.target.port)

rule MSSP_T1071_002_NetDev_FTP_Login_Then_Outbound_Transfer {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects a network device management-plane authentication event followed within 5 minutes by an outbound FTP/TFTP/FTPS flow originating from the same device. Adversaries abuse file-transfer protocols for C2 by authenticating to a network device and then exfiltrating configuration or staging payloads via FTP variants. This rule correlates the login event with the subsequent outbound transfer flow to surface the combined behaviour, which is more indicative of abuse than either event alone."
    mitre_tactic         = "Command and Control"
    mitre_technique      = "T1071.002"
    mitre_technique_name = "Application Layer Protocol: File Transfer Protocols"
    log_prerequisites    = "Requires firewall/perimeter flow telemetry that captures both management-plane authentication events (USER_LOGIN) and network flow records (NETWORK_FLOW) for network devices. Both event types must be normalised to UDM and share a common principal.hostname or principal.ip."
    platform             = "Network Devices"
    log_source           = "firewall"
    false_positives      = "Scheduled configuration backups via TFTP/FTP to authorised jump hosts or NMS servers; firmware upgrade workflows; network monitoring platforms polling device configs; legitimate SFTP/FTPS management sessions from authorised admin subnets."
    tuning_guidance      = "Populate %netdev_allowed_mgmt_sources with authorised management source IPs/subnets. Populate %netdev_allowed_ftp_destinations with known-good backup/NMS server IPs. Raise severity or lower the time window if the environment prohibits all outbound FTP from network devices."

  events:
    // Leg 1: management-plane login to a network device
    $auth.metadata.event_type = "USER_LOGIN"
    $auth.principal.ip != ""
    $auth.target.hostname != ""
    not $auth.principal.ip in %netdev_allowed_mgmt_sources
    $auth.target.hostname = $device_hostname

    // Leg 2: outbound FTP / TFTP / FTPS flow from the same device
    $flow.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_FLOW"
    (
      $flow.target.port = 21 or
      $flow.target.port = 69 or
      $flow.target.port = 990 or
      $flow.target.port = 989
    )
    $flow.network.ip_protocol = "TCP" or $flow.network.ip_protocol = "UDP"
    $flow.principal.hostname = $device_hostname
    not $flow.target.ip in %netdev_allowed_ftp_destinations

    // Chronological ordering: login must precede the outbound transfer
    $auth.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $flow.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $device_hostname over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score          = max(80)
    $mitre_technique_id  = array_distinct("T1071.002")
    $primary_entity      = array_distinct($device_hostname)
    $auth_source_ips     = array_distinct($auth.principal.ip)
    $auth_userids        = array_distinct($auth.target.user.userid)
    $ftp_dest_ips        = array_distinct($flow.target.ip)
    $ftp_dest_ports      = array_distinct($flow.target.port)
    $total_bytes_out     = max($flow.network.sent_bytes)

  condition:
    $auth and $flow
}

    )

rule MSSP_T1071_004_ESXi_DNS_Config_Modification {

    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"

    description = "Detects modification of ESXi DNS resolver configuration files or network configuration settings that could indicate an adversary redirecting DNS resolution to an attacker-controlled server to enable DNS tunneling or C2 over DNS.     mitre_tactic = "Command and Control"
    mitre_technique = "T1071.004"
    mitre_technique_name = "Application Layer Protocol: DNS"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires ESXi hostd or shell telemetry forwarded to Chronicle. SETTING_MODIFICATION or FILE_MODIFICATION events must be generated for ESXi network/DNS configuration changes. Confirm your ESXi syslog forwarding captures configuration state changes."
    platform = "ESXi"
    log_source = "vmware_esxi"
    false_positives = "Authorized infrastructure changes by VMware administrators updating DNS servers during planned maintenance, DHCP-driven DNS updates, or automated configuration management tools (Ansible, vSphere Automation SDK) applying approved network settings."
    tuning_guidance = "Add authorized admin user IDs to %esxi_allowed_config_admins. Add approved change-window hostnames to %esxi_approved_mgmt_hosts. Narrow the time window if change-management windows are predictable."

  events:
    $cfg.metadata.event_type = "SETTING_MODIFICATION"

    (
      $cfg.target.resource.name = /dns/ nocase or
      $cfg.target.resource.name = /nameserver/ nocase or

      $cfg.target.resource.name = /Misc\.HostName/ nocase or

      $cfg.target.resource.name = /\/etc\/hosts$/ nocase
    )

    not $cfg.principal.user.userid in %esxi_allowed_config_admins

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(72)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1071.004")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($cfg.principal.hostname)

rule MSSP_T1071_004_DNS_Tunnel_Beacon_Then_High_Volume_Queries {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects DNS tunneling/beaconing behaviour observable at the network perimeter: a host first generates an unusually long DNS query (indicative of data encoding in subdomains), then within the same window produces a high-frequency burst of DNS queries to the same parent domain. Long subdomain labels are a hallmark of DNS tunneling tools that encode C2 commands or exfiltrated data in the QNAME. The burst pattern distinguishes beaconing from legitimate one-off long queries."
    mitre_tactic = "Command and Control"
    mitre_technique = "T1071.004"
    mitre_technique_name = "Application Layer Protocol: DNS"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires firewall or DNS resolver logs normalised to UDM NETWORK_DNS events. The log source must populate network.dns.questions.name (QNAME) and principal.ip. Query count aggregation requires per-query logging, not summary logs."
    platform = "Windows"
    log_source = "firewall"
    false_positives = "CDN health checks with long CNAMEs, legitimate software update services using long subdomains, DNSSEC-signed zones with large labels, enterprise monitoring tools polling many DNS names rapidly."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good high-volume DNS resolvers (e.g. internal recursive resolvers) to %dns_trusted_resolvers. Add approved CDN or update-service parent domains to %dns_allowed_long_query_domains. Raise the query-count threshold in the outcome comment if the environment has noisy legitimate resolvers."

  events:
    // Event 1: A single DNS query with an unusually long QNAME (>52 chars in
    // the full name), characteristic of base32/base64-encoded tunnel payloads
    // embedded in subdomain labels. Pre-filtered to external queries only.
    $long_q.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_DNS"
    re.len($long_q.network.dns.questions.name) > 52
    // Exclude queries that are clearly internal (short hostnames, .local, .internal)
    not $long_q.network.dns.questions.name = /\.(local|internal|corp|lan)$/ nocase
    not $long_q.principal.ip in %dns_trusted_resolvers
    not $long_q.network.dns.questions.name in %dns_allowed_long_query_domains
    $long_q.principal.ip = $src_ip

    // Event 2: A burst of DNS queries from the same source IP within the window.
    // Pre-filtered identically to avoid joining against all DNS traffic.
    $burst_q.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_DNS"
    not $burst_q.network.dns.questions.name = /\.(local|internal|corp|lan)$/ nocase
    not $burst_q.principal.ip in %dns_trusted_resolvers
    $burst_q.principal.ip = $src_ip

    // Chronological ordering: long query precedes or coincides with burst
    $long_q.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $burst_q.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $src_ip over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(78)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1071.004")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($src_ip)
    $queried_names = array_distinct($burst_q.network.dns.questions.name)
    $long_query_names = array_distinct($long_q.network.dns.questions.name)
    $total_dns_queries = count($burst_q.network.dns.questions.name)
    $max_query_name_len = max(re.len($long_q.network.dns.questions.name))

  condition:
    $long_q and $burst_q and $total_dns_queries > 15
}

rule MSSP_T1071_005_PubSub_Protocol_External_Connection {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "Medium"
    description = "Detects outbound connections to external destinations on ports commonly associated with publish/subscribe messaging protocols (MQTT 1883/8883, AMQP 5671/5672, STOMP 61613/61614, XMPP 5222/5269). Adversaries abuse these protocols to blend C2 traffic with legitimate messaging infrastructure. Firewall/perimeter telemetry only - no process context required."
    mitre_tactic = "Command and Control"
    mitre_technique = "T1071.005"
    mitre_technique_name = "Application Layer Protocol: Publish/Subscribe Protocols"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires firewall or perimeter flow logs with destination IP and destination port populated in UDM. Internal RFC-1918 space must be excluded via reference list."
    platform = "Windows"
    log_source = "firewall"
    false_positives = "IoT device management platforms (AWS IoT, Azure IoT Hub), legitimate enterprise messaging middleware (RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ), CI/CD pipeline event buses, chat applications using XMPP (Jabber clients)."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good external broker IPs or CIDR ranges to %pubsub_allowed_external_brokers. Add internal subnets to %rfc1918_internal. Raise severity if the source host is a server rather than a workstation. Consider correlating with low connection frequency to flag beaconing."

  events:
    $net.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_CONNECTION"

    // MQTT plain: 1883, MQTT TLS: 8883
    // AMQP plain: 5672, AMQP TLS: 5671
    // STOMP plain: 61613, STOMP TLS: 61614
    // XMPP client: 5222, XMPP server: 5269
    (
      $net.target.port = 1883 or
      $net.target.port = 8883 or
      $net.target.port = 5671 or

      $net.target.port = 61614 or
      $net.target.port = 5222 or
      $net.target.port = 5269
    )

    // Exclude internal destinations - reference list covers RFC-1918 and
    // any customer-specific private ranges
    not $net.target.ip in %rfc1918_internal

    // Exclude known-good external pub/sub brokers (e.g. managed IoT endpoints)
    not $net.target.ip in %pubsub_allowed_external_brokers

    // Require a source host to be populated for alerting context
    $net.principal.hostname != ""

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(55)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1071.005")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($net.principal.hostname)
    $destination_ip = array_distinct($net.target.ip)
    $destination_port = array_distinct($net.target.port)

    $net

    mitre_technique_name = "Application Layer Protocol: Publish/Subscribe Protocols"

    platform        = "Linux"
    log_source      = "firewall"
