    (
        $conn.target.port = 1883  or
        $conn.target.port = 8883  or
        $conn.target.port = 5671  or
        $conn.target.port = 5672  or
        $conn.target.port = 61613 or
        $conn.target.port = 61614 or
        $conn.target.port = 5222  or
        $conn.target.port = 5269
    )
    not $conn.target.ip in %rfc1918_internal
    not $conn.target.ip in %allowed_pubsub_brokers
    not $conn.principal.ip in %allowed_pubsub_sources
    $conn.principal.ip = $src_ip
    $conn.target.port  = $dst_port

    // --- Leg 2: sustained flow on the same port from the same source ---
    $flow.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_FLOW"
    (
        $flow.target.port = 1883  or
        $flow.target.port = 8883  or
        $flow.target.port = 5671  or
        $flow.target.port = 5672  or
        $flow.target.port = 61613 or
        $flow.target.port = 61614 or
        $flow.target.port = 5222  or
        $flow.target.port = 5269
    )
    not $flow.target.ip in %rfc1918_internal
    not $flow.target.ip in %allowed_pubsub_brokers
    not $flow.principal.ip in %allowed_pubsub_sources
    $flow.principal.ip = $src_ip
    $flow.target.port  = $dst_port

    // Chronological ordering: connection burst precedes or coincides with flow record
    $conn.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $flow.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $src_ip, $dst_port over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score        = max(72)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1071.005")
    $primary_entity    = array_distinct($src_ip)
    $destination_ips   = array_distinct($flow.target.ip)
    $destination_ports = array_distinct($flow.target.port)
    $connection_count  = count($conn.metadata.id)
    $total_bytes_out   = sum($flow.network.sent_bytes)

  condition:
    $conn and $flow
}

rule MSSP_T1071_001_AppLayer_Protocol_Suspicious_Outbound_Connection {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "Medium"
    description = "Detects outbound network connections from Linux hosts to non-standard ports on common application-layer protocols (HTTP/HTTPS/DNS) or connections to external destinations on unusual high ports. Adversaries abuse application-layer protocols to blend C2 traffic with legitimate traffic. This rule operates on firewall/perimeter telemetry and is additive to endpoint process-launch detections."
    mitre_tactic = "Command and Control"
    mitre_technique = "T1071"
    mitre_technique_name = "Application Layer Protocol"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires firewall or perimeter network flow logs normalised into Chronicle UDM NETWORK_CONNECTION or NETWORK_FLOW events. Source IP must be populated with the internal Linux host address."
    platform = "Linux"
    log_source = "firewall"
    false_positives = "Legitimate applications using non-standard ports (e.g., alternate HTTP proxies, developer services, IoT management). CDN or SaaS services that use high ephemeral ports. Authorised VPN or tunnelling solutions."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good internal source IPs or subnets to %internal_address_space. Add approved external destinations to %approved_external_destinations. Add approved high-port services to %approved_high_port_services. Narrow the port ranges if the environment uses specific alternate ports legitimately."

  events:
    $net.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_CONNECTION"

    // Source must be an internal host (not already excluded as internal-to-internal)
    not $net.principal.ip in %internal_address_space

    // Destination must be external (not RFC-1918 or other internal ranges)
    not $net.target.ip in %internal_address_space

    // Destination must not be an approved external destination
    not $net.target.ip in %approved_external_destinations

    // Detect application-layer protocol abuse: HTTP/HTTPS on non-standard ports
    // OR connections on suspicious high ports commonly used for C2 beaconing
    (
      // HTTP on non-standard port (not 80, 8080, 8000, 8888 which are common alternates)
      (
        $net.target.port != 80 and
        $net.target.port != 443 and
        $net.target.port != 8080 and
        $net.target.port != 8443 and
        $net.target.port != 8000 and
        $net.target.port != 8888 and
        $net.target.port != 53 and
        $net.target.port != 22 and
        $net.target.port != 25 and
        $net.target.port != 587 and
        $net.target.port != 993 and
        $net.target.port != 995 and
        $net.network.application_protocol = "HTTP"
      )
      or
      // HTTPS/TLS on non-standard port
      (
        $net.target.port != 443 and
        $net.target.port != 8443 and
        $net.network.application_protocol = "HTTPS"
      )
      or
      // DNS over non-standard port (DNS tunnelling indicator)
      (
        $net.target.port != 53 and
        $net.target.port != 853 and
        $net.network.application_protocol = "DNS"
      )
      or
      // High ephemeral port range commonly used by C2 frameworks for raw TCP/HTTP beaconing
      (
        $net.target.port >= 49152 and
        $net.target.port <= 65535 and
        not $net.target.port in %approved_high_port_services
      )
    )

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(60)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1071")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($net.principal.ip)
    $destination_ip = array_distinct($net.target.ip)
    $destination_port = array_distinct($net.target.port)
    $application_protocol = array_distinct($net.network.application_protocol)

  condition:
    $net
}

rule MSSP_T1071_002_NetDev_Unusual_Port_Then_HighVolume_Flow {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects a network device initiating an outbound connection on an uncommon application-layer port followed by a high-volume flow from the same source within 5 minutes. This pattern is consistent with C2 beaconing or data exfiltration over a non-standard protocol blending into allowed traffic. Targets network device management-plane and flow telemetry."
    mitre_tactic = "Command and Control"
    mitre_technique = "T1071"
    mitre_technique_name = "Application Layer Protocol"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires firewall or perimeter flow logs normalised to UDM NETWORK_CONNECTION and NETWORK_FLOW. Both event types must include principal.ip, target.ip, target.port, and network.sent_bytes where applicable."
    platform = "Network Devices"
    log_source = "firewall"
    false_positives = "Legitimate management traffic on non-standard ports (e.g. custom HTTPS offloads, vendor telemetry), bulk backup transfers, authorised out-of-band management channels, NTP or syslog to non-standard collectors."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known management destinations to %netdev_allowed_mgmt_destinations. Add sanctioned high-volume transfer destinations to %netdev_allowed_bulk_destinations. Raise the bytes threshold if backup windows generate false positives. Narrow target.port exclusions in %netdev_allowed_nonstandard_ports."

  events:
    // Event 1: outbound connection from a network device source IP on an
    // uncommon port (not 80, 443, 22, 23, 161, 162, 514, 53, 179).
    // Pre-filtered to non-RFC1918 destinations to avoid internal noise.
    $conn.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_CONNECTION"
    $conn.target.port != 80
    $conn.target.port != 443
    $conn.target.port != 22
    $conn.target.port != 23
    $conn.target.port != 161
    $conn.target.port != 162
    $conn.target.port != 514
    $conn.target.port != 53
    $conn.target.port != 179
    $conn.target.port > 1024
    not $conn.target.ip in %netdev_allowed_mgmt_destinations
    not $conn.target.port in %netdev_allowed_nonstandard_ports
    $conn.principal.ip = $src_ip

    // Event 2: high-volume flow from the same source IP to the same
    // external destination, indicating sustained data transfer.
    $flow.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_FLOW"
    $flow.network.sent_bytes > 5000000
    not $flow.target.ip in %netdev_allowed_bulk_destinations
    not $flow.target.ip in %netdev_allowed_mgmt_destinations
    $flow.principal.ip = $src_ip

    // Chronological ordering: connection attempt precedes the bulk flow
    $conn.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $flow.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $src_ip over 5m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(75)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1071")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($src_ip)
    $destination_ips = array_distinct($flow.target.ip)
    $destination_ports = array_distinct($conn.target.port)
    $max_bytes_sent = max($flow.network.sent_bytes)
    $connection_count = count($conn.target.port)

  condition:
    $conn and $flow
}

rule MSSP_T1078_001_Container_Default_Account_Resource_Access {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects cloud audit log events where a well-known container or Kubernetes default service account (e.g., 'default', 'system:serviceaccount:default', 'system:anonymous', 'system:unauthenticated') performs resource access or creation actions. Adversaries abuse default accounts to gain initial access or escalate privileges in container environments without needing to compromise a named identity."
    mitre_tactic = "Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation"
    mitre_technique = "T1078.001"
    mitre_technique_name = "Valid Accounts: Default Accounts"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires cloud control plane audit logs with principal user identity populated. For Kubernetes, requires API server audit logging forwarded to Chronicle. For cloud IaaS, requires provider audit logs (e.g., GCP Audit, AWS CloudTrail, Azure Activity) with service account or IAM identity fields."
    platform = "Containers"
    log_source = "cloud_audit"
    false_positives = "Legitimate workloads running under the default Kubernetes service account in non-production namespaces; initial cluster bootstrapping; managed Kubernetes add-ons that have not been migrated to dedicated service accounts."
    tuning_guidance = "Populate %allowed_default_account_principals with approved default-account identities that are known-good in your environment (e.g., specific bootstrapping accounts). Narrow scope by adding namespace or resource type filters once baseline is established."

  events:
    $cloud.metadata.event_type = "USER_RESOURCE_ACCESS"

    // Match well-known default/anonymous Kubernetes and cloud container service account identities
    $cloud.principal.user.userid = /^(default|system:serviceaccount:default:|system:anonymous|system:unauthenticated|service-account-default|root|admin|administrator|kubernetes-admin)/ nocase

    // Exclude explicitly approved default account identities via reference list
    not $cloud.principal.user.userid in %allowed_default_account_principals

    // Require a meaningful target resource to reduce noise from health-check calls
    $cloud.target.resource.name != ""

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(72)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1078.001")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($cloud.principal.hostname)
    $acting_identity = array_distinct($cloud.principal.user.userid)
    $accessed_resource = array_distinct($cloud.target.resource.name)
    $resource_type = array_distinct($cloud.target.resource.resource_type)

  condition:
    $cloud
}

rule MSSP_T1078_001_Default_Account_Login_Then_Config_Change_NetworkDevice {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects a successful management-plane login from an external or unexpected source using a well-known default account username, followed by a configuration modification on the same network device within 1 hour. This pattern is consistent with adversaries leveraging default credentials on network appliances to gain access and then alter device configuration for persistence or lateral movement."
    mitre_tactic = "Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation"
    mitre_technique = "T1078.001"
    mitre_technique_name = "Valid Accounts: Default Accounts"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires network device syslog or management-plane authentication logs normalised to UDM USER_LOGIN, and configuration change events normalised to UDM SETTING_MODIFICATION. Both event types must populate principal.hostname (device) and principal.user.userid."
    platform = "Network Devices"
    log_source = "firewall"
    false_positives = "Legitimate network administrators who have not renamed default accounts; automated provisioning systems using factory credentials during initial device bring-up; vendor support sessions using default service accounts."
    tuning_guidance = "Populate %allowed_mgmt_source_ips with approved management station IPs/ranges to suppress known-good sources. Populate %allowed_default_account_names if your environment legitimately retains any default account names. Narrow the match window if 1h produces too many false positives in high-change environments."

  events:
    // Event 1: Successful login to the network device management plane
    // using a username that matches common default account patterns
    $auth.metadata.event_type = "USER_LOGIN"
    $auth.principal.user.userid = /^(admin|administrator|root|cisco|enable|guest|operator|manager|support|service|default|netadmin|superuser|ubnt|pi|user|test|demo|setup|recovery|backup|monitor|readonly|ro|rw|sysadmin|netscreen|admin1|Admin)$/ nocase
    not $auth.principal.ip in %allowed_mgmt_source_ips
    not $auth.principal.user.userid in %allowed_default_account_names
    $auth.target.hostname = $device_hostname

    // Event 2: Configuration change on the same device after the login
    $cfg.metadata.event_type = "SETTING_MODIFICATION"
    $cfg.principal.user.userid = $auth.principal.user.userid
    $cfg.target.hostname = $device_hostname

    // Enforce chronological ordering: login must precede config change
    $auth.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $cfg.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $device_hostname over 1h

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(82)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1078.001")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($device_hostname)
    $default_account_used = array_distinct($auth.principal.user.userid)
    $source_ips = array_distinct($auth.principal.ip)
    $config_changes = count($cfg.metadata.id)
    $earliest_login_ts = min($auth.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds)
    $latest_change_ts = max($cfg.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds)

  condition:
    $auth and $cfg
}

rule MSSP_T1078_002_Domain_Account_SSH_AuthorizedKeys_Modification {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Single-Event"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects file creation or modification of SSH authorized_keys files outside of expected administrative tooling. Adversaries who obtain domain account credentials on Linux systems frequently persist by injecting their own public key into an existing user's authorized_keys file, enabling password-free re-entry even after a credential rotation. This rule targets the resulting file artifact rather than the command used to write it, providing a detection layer that survives command-line obfuscation."
    mitre_tactic    = "Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Initial Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1078.002"
    mitre_technique_name = "Valid Accounts: Domain Accounts"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires Linux EDR or auditd file-write telemetry normalised into Chronicle UDM FILE_CREATION or FILE_MODIFICATION events. Auditd rule '-w /root/.ssh -p wa' and equivalent per-user rules, or EDR file monitoring covering /home/*/.ssh/ and /root/.ssh/, must be active."
    platform        = "Linux"
    log_source      = "linux_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Legitimate SSH key deployment by configuration management tools (Ansible, Puppet, Chef, Terraform), provisioning scripts, or authorized administrators manually adding keys. Cloud-init on first boot may also trigger this rule."
    tuning_guidance = "Add the full paths of approved configuration management agent binaries (e.g. /usr/bin/ansible, /opt/puppet/bin/puppet) to %linux_allowed_ssh_key_writers. Consider also scoping by time-of-day if key deployment is restricted to maintenance windows."

  events:
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_MODIFICATION"

    // Target the authorized_keys artifact in any user home directory or root
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\/(root|home\/[^\/]+)\/.ssh\/authorized_keys(2)?$/ nocase

    // Exclude known-good configuration management and provisioning processes
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %linux_allowed_ssh_key_writers

    // Exclude the sshd daemon itself performing internal key cache operations
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\/sbin\/sshd$/ nocase

    // Exclude system package managers performing legitimate file placement
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\/(usr\/bin\/(dpkg|rpm|yum|dnf|apt)|bin\/rpm)$/ nocase

  outcome:
    $risk_score        = max(80)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1078.002")
    $primary_entity    = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)
    $modified_key_file = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $writing_process   = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $acting_user       = array_distinct($file.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $file
}

rule MSSP_T1078_002_ESXi_Domain_Account_Login_Then_Setting_Change {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects a domain account authenticating to an ESXi host followed by a host-level setting modification within 1 hour. Adversaries who compromise domain credentials may leverage them to authenticate to ESXi management interfaces and then alter host configuration to establish persistence or facilitate VM manipulation. This correlation provides additive coverage beyond command-line process-launch detections."
    mitre_tactic = "Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation"
    mitre_technique = "T1078.002"
    mitre_technique_name = "Valid Accounts: Domain Accounts"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires ESXi hostd authentication logs normalised to USER_LOGIN UDM events and ESXi host configuration change events normalised to SETTING_MODIFICATION. Both must be ingested via the vmware_esxi log source."
    platform = "ESXi"
    log_source = "vmware_esxi"
    false_positives = "Authorised vSphere administrators performing routine maintenance, automated configuration management tools (e.g. Ansible, vRealize Automation) using domain service accounts, scheduled compliance remediation jobs."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good domain service account userids to %esxi_allowed_domain_service_accounts. Add authorised management hostnames to %esxi_allowed_mgmt_hosts. Narrow the time window if false-positive volume remains high."

  events:
    // Event 1: Domain account login to ESXi host
    $auth.metadata.event_type = "USER_LOGIN"
    // Domain accounts are distinguished by a UPN or DOMAIN\user format
    $auth.target.user.userid = /[@\\]/ nocase
    // Exclude known-good domain service accounts
    not $auth.target.user.userid in %esxi_allowed_domain_service_accounts
    // Exclude known authorised management source hosts
    not $auth.principal.hostname in %esxi_allowed_mgmt_hosts
    // Bind the ESXi host being logged into as the join key
    $auth.target.hostname = $esxi_host
    // Bind the authenticated user as a secondary join key to avoid cross-user false positives
    $auth.target.user.userid = $domain_user

    // Event 2: Host-level setting modification on the same ESXi host
    $cfg.metadata.event_type = "SETTING_MODIFICATION"
    $cfg.target.hostname = $esxi_host
    $cfg.principal.user.userid = $domain_user
    // Exclude known-good domain service accounts (mirror of auth filter)
    not $cfg.principal.user.userid in %esxi_allowed_domain_service_accounts

    // Enforce chronological ordering: login must precede the config change
    $auth.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $cfg.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $esxi_host, $domain_user over 1h

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(80)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1078.002")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($esxi_host)
    $affected_user = array_distinct($domain_user)
    $auth_source_hosts = array_distinct($auth.principal.hostname)
    $modified_settings = array_distinct($cfg.target.resource.name)
    $login_count = count($auth.metadata.id)
    $setting_change_count = count($cfg.metadata.id)

  condition:
    $auth and $cfg
}

rule MSSP_T1078_003_Local_Account_Auth_Anomaly {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects successful authentication events from local accounts (non-domain, non-service accounts) that exhibit anomalous characteristics: authentication outside business hours, use of built-in privileged local accounts, or authentication to sensitive resources. Targets the resulting authentication state change rather than the process-creation layer, providing additive coverage over command-line rules."
    mitre_tactic = "Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation"
    mitre_technique = "T1078.003"
    mitre_technique_name = "Valid Accounts: Local Accounts"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires identity provider or directory audit logs normalised to UDM USER_LOGIN events. Covers on-premises AD authentication logs forwarded to Chronicle, or equivalent identity telemetry. Local account logins are identified by the absence of a domain suffix or UPN and presence of a local machine context."
    platform = "Windows"
    log_source = "identity"
    false_positives = "Break-glass / emergency local admin accounts used during outages, legitimate local service accounts, IT helpdesk performing authorised local admin tasks, automated patching agents using local credentials."
    tuning_guidance = "Add approved local service account usernames to %allowed_local_service_accounts. Add approved administrator workstation hostnames to %allowed_local_admin_hosts. Restrict the built-in account name regex if your environment uses non-standard naming. Consider narrowing the hour-of-day window to match your organisation's business hours."

  events:
    $auth.metadata.event_type = "USER_LOGIN"

    // Target local accounts: no UPN domain component, no Kerberos realm indicator.
    // Local accounts typically have no '@' in the userid or have a bare username.
    not $auth.target.user.userid = /@/ nocase

    // Exclude machine accounts (end with $) which are normal domain computer auth.
    not $auth.target.user.userid = /\$$/ nocase

    // Exclude well-known non-interactive system identities.
    not $auth.target.user.userid = /^(system|network service|local service|anonymous logon|iis apppool)$/ nocase

    // Flag use of built-in privileged local account names that adversaries commonly
    // target or re-enable. Matches Administrator, admin, Guest (re-enabled), and
    // common default local admin naming conventions without hardcoding exact names.
    (
      $auth.target.user.userid = /^(administrator|admin|guest|defaultaccount|wdagutilityaccount)$/ nocase
      or
      // Catch renamed-but-common local admin patterns (e.g. ladmin, localadmin, adm_*)
      $auth.target.user.userid = /^(l\.?admin|local[\._-]?admin|adm[\._-])/ nocase
    )

    // Require a successful login outcome - we want the resulting access, not failed attempts.
    $auth.security_result.action = "ALLOW"

    // Exclude known-approved local service accounts and approved hosts.
    not $auth.target.user.userid in %allowed_local_service_accounts
    not $auth.principal.hostname in %allowed_local_admin_hosts

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(72)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1078.003")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($auth.principal.hostname)
    $local_account_used = array_distinct($auth.target.user.userid)
    $source_ip = array_distinct($auth.principal.ip)

  condition:
    $auth
}

rule MSSP_T1078_003_Local_Account_Created_Then_Login {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects a new local account creation event followed by a successful interactive or remote login from that same account within 1 hour on Linux. This sequence is indicative of an adversary establishing persistence via a local account and immediately leveraging it for access, rather than a routine admin workflow where login would typically be delayed or absent."
    mitre_tactic = "Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Initial Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1078.003"
    mitre_technique_name = "Valid Accounts: Local Accounts"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires Linux EDR or auditd telemetry normalised to Chronicle UDM. Account creation events must populate target.user.userid. Login events must populate target.user.userid and metadata.event_type = USER_LOGIN. Auditd rules for execve (useradd/adduser) and PAM/sshd login events must be active."
    platform = "Linux"
    log_source = "linux_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Automated provisioning pipelines (Ansible, Terraform, cloud-init) that create accounts and immediately validate them; container entrypoint scripts that create service accounts at startup; CI/CD agents bootstrapping ephemeral build environments."
    tuning_guidance = "Add provisioning service account names to %linux_allowed_provisioning_users. Add known automation hostnames to %linux_allowed_automation_hosts. Narrow the time window if false-positive rate remains high in environments with heavy automation."

  events:
    // Event 1: Local account creation via useradd or adduser
    $create.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_LAUNCH"
    $create.target.process.file.full_path = /\/(useradd|adduser)$/ nocase
    // Capture the newly created username from the command line (last non-flag token)
    $create.target.process.command_line = /useradd|adduser/ nocase
    // Exclude known provisioning accounts and automation hosts
    not $create.principal.user.userid in %linux_allowed_provisioning_users
    not $create.principal.hostname in %linux_allowed_automation_hosts
    // Extract the hostname as the join key
    $create.principal.hostname = $hostname
    // Extract the created username from the command line for joining
    // The new account name appears as the last argument; capture via a broad match
    // We join on the target user created - populated by EDR normalisation
    $create.target.user.userid = $new_userid

    // Event 2: Successful login by that same newly created account
    $login.metadata.event_type = "USER_LOGIN"
    $login.target.user.userid = $new_userid
    $login.principal.hostname = $hostname
    not $login.target.user.userid in %linux_allowed_provisioning_users
    not $login.principal.hostname in %linux_allowed_automation_hosts

    // Chronological ordering: account creation must precede the login
    $create.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $login.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname, $new_userid over 1h

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(80)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1078.003")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($hostname)
    $created_account = array_distinct($new_userid)
    $creation_cmdline = array_distinct($create.target.process.command_line)
    $login_source_ip = array_distinct($login.principal.ip)

rule MSSP_T1078_004_SaaS_Cloud_Account_Privilege_Escalation_Via_Role_Change {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects privilege escalation or persistence via cloud account role or permission changes in identity provider audit logs. Adversaries who have compromised a cloud account may elevate its privileges by assigning administrative roles or modifying group memberships to maintain access and expand their footprint across SaaS and IaaS resources."
    mitre_tactic = "Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Initial Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1078.004"
    mitre_technique_name = "Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires identity provider audit logs (e.g., Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace) normalised to Chronicle UDM. Must capture USER_CHANGE_PERMISSIONS and GROUP_MODIFICATION events including the actor, target user, and role/group name."
    platform = "SaaS"
    log_source = "identity"
    false_positives = "Authorised IT provisioning workflows, HR onboarding automation, break-glass account activation, approved role reviews performed by identity governance tooling."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known provisioning service accounts to %idp_approved_provisioning_accounts. Add approved administrative role names to %idp_approved_admin_roles if your environment uses a fixed set of privileged roles. Scope alerts to changes outside business hours or originating from unexpected IP ranges for higher fidelity."

  events:
    $auth.metadata.event_type = "USER_CHANGE_PERMISSIONS"
    // Target a user whose permissions are being elevated
    $auth.target.user.userid != ""
    // Actor performing the change must be present
    $auth.principal.user.userid != ""
    // Detect assignment of highly privileged roles by matching common admin role name patterns
    // Covers: Global Admin, Company Admin, Privileged Role Admin, Super Admin, Org Admin, etc.
    $auth.target.user.attribute.roles.name = /global.?admin|company.?admin|privileged.?role|super.?admin|org.?admin|directory.?admin|security.?admin|exchange.?admin|sharepoint.?admin|teams.?admin|billing.?admin|application.?admin|cloud.?admin|owner/ nocase
    // Exclude self-service role assignments that are expected (actor != target)
    // and exclude known provisioning accounts
    not $auth.principal.user.userid in %idp_approved_provisioning_accounts
    // Exclude changes where the actor and target are the same service identity (self-assignment noise)
    $auth.principal.user.userid != $auth.target.user.userid

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(80)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1078.004")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($auth.target.user.userid)
    $actor_userid = array_distinct($auth.principal.user.userid)
    $assigned_role = array_distinct($auth.target.user.attribute.roles.name)

  condition:
    $auth
}

rule MSSP_T1078_004_Cloud_Account_Login_Then_Privilege_Escalation {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects a cloud identity account that successfully authenticates and then, within one hour, is granted elevated permissions or added to a privileged group. This pattern is consistent with an adversary leveraging a compromised cloud account to escalate privileges or establish persistence via role/group manipulation."
    mitre_tactic    = "Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation"
    mitre_technique = "T1078.004"
    mitre_technique_name = "Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires identity provider sign-in logs (successful authentications) and directory audit logs capturing permission changes and group membership modifications. Both must be ingested and normalized to UDM."
    platform        = "IaaS"
    log_source      = "identity"
    false_positives = "Legitimate IT onboarding workflows where a new account is provisioned and immediately granted access; automated provisioning pipelines; break-glass account activation by authorized administrators; scheduled role-assignment automation."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known provisioning service accounts to %cloud_privileged_provisioning_accounts. Add known automation principals to %cloud_automation_principals. Narrow the match window if false-positive rates are high in environments with frequent automated role assignments."

  events:
    // Event 1: Successful cloud identity authentication
    $auth.metadata.event_type = "USER_LOGIN"
    $auth.security_result.summary = /success/ nocase
    $auth.principal.user.userid = $cloud_userid
    not $auth.principal.user.userid in %cloud_privileged_provisioning_accounts
    not $auth.principal.user.userid in %cloud_automation_principals

    // Event 2: Privilege escalation - permission change or group modification
    // targeting the same user identity that just authenticated
    (
      $priv.metadata.event_type = "USER_CHANGE_PERMISSIONS" or
      $priv.metadata.event_type = "GROUP_MODIFICATION"
    )
    // The beneficiary of the privilege change is the account that just logged in
    $priv.target.user.userid = $cloud_userid
    // Filter to high-value privilege operations only
    (
      $priv.target.resource.name = /admin|owner|contributor|privileged|global|superuser|root|poweruser|securityadmin|roleadmin/ nocase or
      $priv.security_result.summary = /admin|owner|contributor|privileged|global|superuser|root|poweruser|securityadmin|roleadmin/ nocase
    )
    not $priv.principal.user.userid in %cloud_privileged_provisioning_accounts
    not $priv.principal.user.userid in %cloud_automation_principals

    // Chronological ordering: login must precede privilege change
    $auth.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $priv.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $cloud_userid over 1h

  outcome:
    $risk_score          = max(80)
    $mitre_technique_id  = array_distinct("T1078.004")
    $primary_entity      = array_distinct($cloud_userid)
    $auth_event_count    = count($auth.metadata.id)
    $priv_event_count    = count($priv.metadata.id)
    $privilege_targets   = array_distinct($priv.target.resource.name)
    $granting_principals = array_distinct($priv.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $auth and $priv
}

rule MSSP_T1078_001_SaaS_Dormant_Account_Login_Anomaly {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Single-Event"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects a successful authentication event from an account that has not been seen logging in recently, combined with indicators of privilege escalation or sensitive resource access. Adversaries abusing valid accounts — including dormant or former-employee accounts — will produce an authentication event in identity-provider audit logs. This rule pivots on the USER_LOGIN telemetry layer rather than process-creation, providing additive coverage over existing command-line detections."
    mitre_tactic    = "Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Defense Evasion"
    mitre_technique = "T1078"
    mitre_technique_name = "Valid Accounts"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires identity-provider sign-in audit logs normalised to UDM USER_LOGIN events. Fields required: principal.user.userid, principal.user.account_type, target.resource.name, security_result.summary, extensions.auth.auth_details, network.ip_protocol. MFA outcome and risk signals must be present in security_result."
    platform        = "SaaS"
    log_source      = "identity"
    false_positives = "Legitimate users returning from extended leave, shared service accounts used infrequently, automated service-principal logins, break-glass admin accounts used during incidents."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known break-glass or service accounts to %idp_allowed_dormant_accounts. Add approved admin user IDs to %idp_privileged_account_allowlist. Raise the risk_score threshold if the environment has many infrequent-login users (e.g., contractors). Consider narrowing to specific sensitive target resources via %idp_sensitive_resource_patterns."

  events:
    $auth.metadata.event_type = "USER_LOGIN"

    // Successful authentication only — failed logins are a separate detection
    $auth.security_result.summary = /success|succeeded|authenticated/ nocase

    // Target a privileged or administrative account type, or an account
    // flagged as high-risk by the identity provider's own risk engine.
    // This catches both direct admin abuse and risk-elevated sign-ins.
    (
      $auth.principal.user.account_type = "ADMINISTRATOR" or
      $auth.security_result.summary = /risk.*high|high.*risk|atypical|anomalous|unfamiliar/ nocase
    )

    // MFA was either not satisfied or was bypassed — a strong signal of
    // credential abuse rather than a legitimate owner logging in.
    // Identity providers surface this in auth_details or summary.
    $auth.extensions.auth.auth_details = /mfa.*bypass|no.*mfa|mfa.*not.*required|single.*factor|legacy.*auth|basic.*auth/ nocase

    // Exclude known-good dormant or service accounts managed by the MSSP
    not $auth.principal.user.userid in %idp_allowed_dormant_accounts

    // Exclude approved privileged accounts that legitimately skip MFA
    not $auth.principal.user.userid in %idp_privileged_account_allowlist

    // Capture the user for grouping and outcome
    $auth.principal.user.userid = $userid

  outcome:
    $risk_score        = max(82)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1078")
    $primary_entity    = array_distinct($auth.principal.user.userid)
    $target_resource   = array_distinct($auth.target.resource.name)
    $source_ip         = array_distinct($auth.principal.ip)
    $auth_details      = array_distinct($auth.extensions.auth.auth_details)
    $account_type      = array_distinct($auth.principal.user.account_type)

  condition:
    $auth
}

rule MSSP_T1078_IaaS_Impossible_Travel_Then_Privilege_Change {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects a valid-account abuse pattern on IaaS identity providers: a successful login from an unexpected or foreign country code is followed within 1 hour by a privilege or group change performed by the same user. This two-stage sequence is a strong indicator of compromised credentials being used to escalate access, as seen in cloud account takeover campaigns."
    mitre_tactic    = "Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation"
    mitre_technique = "T1078"
    mitre_technique_name = "Valid Accounts"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires identity provider sign-in logs (e.g., Entra ID Sign-in Logs, Okta System Log) and directory audit logs normalised to Chronicle UDM. Sign-in events must populate network.ip_geo_artifact.location.country_or_region or principal.ip_geo_artifact.location.country_or_region. Privilege change events must produce USER_CHANGE_PERMISSIONS or GROUP_MODIFICATION."
    platform        = "IaaS"
    log_source      = "identity"
    false_positives = "Administrators travelling internationally and performing legitimate role assignments; automated service accounts with geo-distributed infrastructure; VPN exit nodes that appear as foreign countries."
    tuning_guidance = "Populate %allowed_admin_userids with break-glass and service accounts that legitimately perform cross-geo privilege changes. Populate %allowed_country_codes with countries approved for administrative access in your organisation. Narrow $auth.network.ip_geo_artifact.location.country_or_region exclusions to reduce noise from known VPN egress countries."

  events:
    // Event 1: Successful login from a country NOT in the approved list
    $auth.metadata.event_type = "USER_LOGIN"
    $auth.security_result.summary = /success/ nocase
    not $auth.network.ip_geo_artifact.location.country_or_region in %allowed_country_codes
    $auth.principal.user.userid = $userid
    not $auth.principal.user.userid in %allowed_admin_userids

    // Event 2: Privilege or group change by the same user within the window
    $priv.metadata.event_type = "USER_CHANGE_PERMISSIONS"
    $priv.principal.user.userid = $userid
    not $priv.principal.user.userid in %allowed_admin_userids

    // Chronological ordering: login must precede the privilege change
    $auth.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $priv.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $userid over 1h

  outcome:
    $risk_score          = max(85)
    $mitre_technique_id  = array_distinct("T1078")
    $primary_entity      = array_distinct($userid)
    $login_country       = array_distinct($auth.network.ip_geo_artifact.location.country_or_region)
    $login_source_ip     = array_distinct($auth.principal.ip)
    $privilege_target    = array_distinct($priv.target.user.userid)
    $login_count         = count($auth.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds)
    $priv_change_count   = count($priv.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds)

  condition:
    $auth and $priv
}

rule MSSP_T1105_ESXi_Ingress_Tool_File_Creation {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects creation of new files in writable ESXi filesystem locations commonly used by adversaries to stage ingress tool transfers (e.g. /tmp, /var/run, scratch datastores). Targets the file artifact produced by wget, curl, scp, or sftp rather than the command line, providing coverage when process telemetry is absent or evaded."
    mitre_tactic = "Command and Control"
    mitre_technique = "T1105"
    mitre_technique_name = "Ingress Tool Transfer"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires ESXi shell/hostd file-activity telemetry normalised into Chronicle UDM FILE_CREATION events. Typically sourced from VMware ESXi syslog forwarding or an EDR agent capable of monitoring ESXi file system events."
    platform = "ESXi"
    log_source = "vmware_esxi"
    false_positives = "Legitimate administrator-initiated file transfers for patching or VIB installation, automated backup agents writing to scratch volumes, VMware Update Manager staging files."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good staging directories or authorised admin user accounts to %esxi_allowed_staging_paths and %esxi_allowed_transfer_users respectively. Narrow scope by correlating with preceding USER_LOGIN events from unexpected source IPs."

  events:
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"

    // Target writable ESXi paths used for tool staging:
    // /tmp, /var/run, /var/log (abuse), /scratch, /vmfs/volumes datastore roots
    $file.target.file.full_path = /^(\/tmp\/|\/var\/run\/|\/var\/tmp\/|\/scratch\/|\/vmfs\/volumes\/[^\/]+\/[^\/]+\/)/ nocase

    // Exclude known benign ESXi runtime file patterns (lock files, pid files, vmware temp artefacts)
    not $file.target.file.full_path = /\.(lck|pid|vmsd|vmx\.lck|hib|vswp|vmem)$/ nocase

    // Exclude known VMware internal writers
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\/(bin|sbin|lib)\/(hostd|vpxa|vmkiscsid|storageRM|rhttpproxy|vmsyslogd|fdm)$/ nocase

    // Exclude paths explicitly allow-listed by the MSSP operator
    not $file.target.file.full_path in %esxi_allowed_staging_paths

    // Exclude authorised transfer accounts (e.g. vcenter service accounts)
    not $file.principal.user.userid in %esxi_allowed_transfer_users

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(72)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1105")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)
    $staged_file_path = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $acting_user = array_distinct($file.principal.user.userid)
    $writing_process = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)

  condition:
    $file
}

rule MSSP_T1555_002_Securityd_Memory_Proc_Mem_File_Access {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "Critical"
    description = "Detects file read or open access to /proc/<pid>/mem or /proc/<pid>/maps targeting a process that may be securityd or a credential-caching daemon. On Linux, adversaries with root access can read another process's virtual memory via the /proc filesystem to extract cached credentials. This rule fires on FILE_READ events against /proc/*/mem or /proc/*/maps paths, which is the artifact-layer indicator that memory scraping is occurring, distinct from the process-launch command used to initiate it."
    mitre_tactic = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1555.002"
    mitre_technique_name = "Credentials from Password Stores: Securityd Memory"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires Linux EDR or auditd with file-open/read syscall auditing enabled (audit rules for -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S open,openat,read -F path=/proc). Chronicle UDM FILE_READ events must be populated with target.file.full_path."
    platform = "Linux"
    log_source = "linux_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Legitimate debuggers (gdb, strace, lldb) used by developers; system monitoring agents (Datadog, Dynatrace, New Relic) that inspect process memory; kernel crash dump utilities; authorized security scanners. These should be added to the exclusion list."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known monitoring agent binary paths to %linux_allowed_proc_mem_readers. Narrow scope further by correlating the reading process's effective UID to 0 (root) if your EDR populates principal.user.userid."

  events:
    $open.metadata.event_type = "FILE_READ"
    $open.target.file.full_path = /\/proc\/[0-9]+\/(mem|maps|environ|fd)$/ nocase
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path in %linux_allowed_proc_mem_readers
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\/(usr\/bin\/strace|usr\/bin\/gdb|usr\/bin\/ltrace|usr\/lib\/systemd\/systemd)$/

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(90)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1555.002")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($open.principal.hostname)
    $reading_process = array_distinct($open.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $target_proc_path = array_distinct($open.target.file.full_path)
    $acting_user = array_distinct($open.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $open
}

rule MSSP_T1555_002_Securityd_Memory_Proc_Read_Then_File_Drop {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects a two-stage credential harvesting pattern on Linux: first, a process opens /proc/<pid>/mem or /proc/<pid>/maps of a security-related daemon (e.g. gnome-keyring-daemon, dbus-daemon, or similar credential-caching services) to read its memory, followed within 10 minutes by a file creation in a world-writable or temporary directory on the same host. This sequence is consistent with T1555.002 memory-scraping behaviour adapted to Linux credential stores."
    mitre_tactic    = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1555.002"
    mitre_technique_name = "Credentials from Password Stores: Securityd Memory"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires Linux EDR or auditd telemetry normalised to Chronicle UDM. Auditd rules must capture openat/open syscalls on /proc paths (AUDIT_SYSCALL) and file creation events. EDR agents must emit FILE_READ and FILE_CREATION events."
    platform        = "Linux"
    log_source      = "linux_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Legitimate debuggers (gdb, strace, ltrace) attached to keyring daemons by authorised developers; system monitoring agents reading /proc for health checks; crash dump collectors; container runtime introspection tools."
    tuning_guidance = "Add authorised monitoring agent paths to %linux_allowed_proc_readers. Add approved staging directories to %linux_allowed_output_dirs. Consider narrowing $open.target.file.full_path to match only the specific daemon PID directories if your EDR resolves them."

  events:
    // Stage 1: A process reads /proc/<pid>/mem or /proc/<pid>/maps of a
    // credential-caching daemon. We match on the file path pattern rather
    // than a specific PID because PIDs are ephemeral.
    $open.metadata.event_type = "FILE_READ"
    $open.target.file.full_path = /\/proc\/[0-9]+\/(mem|maps|environ|fd)$/ nocase
    $open.principal.process.file.full_path = /\/(gnome-keyring-daemon|dbus-daemon|polkitd|pam|sssd|lsass|seahorse|kwallet|keepassxc|gpg-agent)/ nocase
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path in %linux_allowed_proc_readers
    $open.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Stage 2: Within the same window, a file is created in a temp or
    // world-writable location on the same host, consistent with staging
    // harvested credentials for exfiltration.
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_CREATION"
    $file.target.file.full_path = /^\/(tmp|dev\/shm|var\/tmp|run\/user\/[0-9]+|proc\/[0-9]+\/fd)/ nocase
    not $file.target.file.full_path in %linux_allowed_output_dirs
    $file.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Chronological ordering: memory read must precede the file drop
    $open.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $file.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname over 10m

  outcome:
    $risk_score          = max(82)
    $mitre_technique_id  = array_distinct("T1555.002")
    $primary_entity      = array_distinct($hostname)
    $reading_process     = array_distinct($open.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $proc_path_accessed  = array_distinct($open.target.file.full_path)
    $staged_file_paths   = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $acting_user         = array_distinct($open.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $open and $file
}

rule MSSP_T1555_003_Browser_Credential_DB_File_Read {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Single-Event"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects file-read or file-open access to browser credential database files on Linux (e.g., Chrome Login Data, Firefox key4.db / logins.json, Chromium-based Login Data). This rule pivots on the FILE_READ artifact rather than process command-line arguments, providing coverage against attackers who avoid noisy process invocations or use memory-only tooling to open the credential store directly."
    mitre_tactic    = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1555.003"
    mitre_technique_name = "Credentials from Web Browsers"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires Linux EDR or auditd with file-open/read syscall auditing enabled (auditd rules targeting -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S open,openat -F exit=-EACCES or equivalent). Chronicle UDM FILE_READ events must be populated with target.file.full_path and principal.process.file.full_path."
    platform        = "Linux"
    log_source      = "linux_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Browser sync daemons, backup agents (e.g., Bacula, Veeam Linux agent), password manager integrations (e.g., KeePassXC browser plugin), legitimate user-initiated browser profile exports, IT asset management tools reading browser profiles."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good backup or sync process paths to %linux_allowed_browser_db_readers. Narrow scope further by excluding reads where principal.user.userid matches the owning user of the profile directory if your EDR populates that field reliably. Consider raising severity to Critical when the reading process is not a known browser binary."

  events:
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_READ"

    // Target: browser credential database files across common Linux browser profile paths.
    // Covers Chrome, Chromium, Brave, Edge-Linux, Vivaldi (Login Data),
    // Firefox / Librewolf (key4.db, logins.json, signons.sqlite),
    // and Opera (Login Data).
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\/(\.config|\.mozilla|snap\/chromium|snap\/firefox|\.local\/share)\// nocase

    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\/(chrome|chromium|brave|msedge|opera|vivaldi|firefox|librewolf|waterfox)$/ nocase

    // Exclude known-good tooling via reference list for multi-tenant tuning.
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %linux_allowed_browser_db_readers

    // Exclude root-owned system maintenance processes that legitimately traverse home dirs.
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\/(rsync|tar|find|locate|updatedb|bacula-fd|veeamsnap)$/ nocase

  outcome:
    $risk_score        = max(80)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1555.003")
    $primary_entity    = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)
    $accessing_process = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $credential_file   = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $acting_user       = array_distinct($file.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $file
}

rule MSSP_T1555_003_BrowserCredDB_Read_Then_Network {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects a non-browser process opening a browser credential database file (Chrome Login Data, Firefox logins.json, Edge Login Data, etc.) followed by an outbound network connection from the same process on the same host within 10 minutes.     mitre_tactic = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1555.003"
    mitre_technique_name = "Credentials from Web Browsers"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR file-read/open telemetry and network connection telemetry normalised into UDM FILE_READ and NETWORK_CONNECTION events. Sysmon Event IDs 11/23 (file) and 3 (network) or equivalent EDR telemetry."
    platform = "Windows"
    log_source = "windows_endpoint"

  events:

    $file.target.file.full_path = /\\AppData\\(Local|Roaming)\\(Google\\Chrome|Microsoft\\Edge|Mozilla\\Firefox|BraveSoftware\\Brave-Browser|Opera Software\\Opera Stable)\\(User Data\\[^\\]+\\Login Data|Profiles\\[^\\]+\\logins\.json|User Data\\[^\\]+\\Web Data)/ nocase
    // Exclude the browsers themselves from triggering
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|opera)\.exe$/ nocase
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_browser_db_readers
    $file.principal.hostname = $hostname
    $file.principal.process.file.full_path = $accessor_proc

    // Event 2: The same process path makes an outbound network connection
    $net.metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_CONNECTION"
    $net.principal.process.file.full_path = $accessor_proc
    not $net.target.ip in %rfc1918_internal
    not $net.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_browser_db_readers
    $net.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Enforce chronological ordering: file read before network connection
    $file.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $net.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname, $accessor_proc over 10m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(85)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1555.003")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)
    $accessing_process = array_distinct($accessor_proc)
    $credential_files_accessed = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $destination_ips = array_distinct($net.target.ip)
    $destination_ports = array_distinct($net.target.port)
    $affected_user = array_distinct($file.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $file and $net
}

rule MSSP_T1555_004_CredentialVault_File_Read {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Single-Event"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects file read access to Windows Credential Locker artifacts (.vcrd files and Policy.vpol) stored under user AppData paths. Adversaries accessing these files are attempting to extract encrypted credentials from the Windows Credential Manager. This rule fires on the file-access event rather than the process command line, providing coverage that evades command-line logging gaps."
    mitre_tactic = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1555.004"
    mitre_technique_name = "Credentials from Password Stores: Windows Credential Manager"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR or Sysmon file-access telemetry (Sysmon Event ID 11 or equivalent EDR file-read events normalised to FILE_READ in UDM). Object access auditing must be enabled for the Vault/Credentials directories."
    platform = "Windows"
    log_source = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Windows LSASS or credential backup utilities performing legitimate vault maintenance. Windows Hello provisioning. Enterprise password managers with vault integration. Backup agents traversing AppData."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good backup agent process paths to %global_allowed_vault_readers. If LSASS generates noise, add its full path. Scope by principal.user.userid to exclude service accounts that legitimately access vault files."

  events:
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_READ"
    // Target the Credential Locker file artifacts: .vcrd credential blobs and Policy.vpol encryption key
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\(Vault|Credentials)\\.*\.(vcrd|vpol)$/ nocase
    // Exclude the Windows OS processes that legitimately manage vault files
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\Windows\\System32\\lsass\.exe$/ nocase
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\Windows\\System32\\svchost\.exe$/ nocase
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\Windows\\System32\\vaultsvc\.dll$/ nocase
    // Reference-list exclusion for known-good administrative and backup tooling
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_vault_readers

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(80)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1555.004")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)
    $accessing_process = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $vault_file_accessed = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $user_context = array_distinct($file.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $file
}

rule MSSP_T1555_004_CredMgr_Vault_File_Read_After_Enum {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects a two-stage Windows Credential Manager harvesting pattern: first a process enumerates credential vaults (via vaultcmd.exe or a PowerShell CredentialManager API call), then within 10 minutes a process reads or opens the encrypted vault credential files (.vcrd) or the vault policy file (Policy.vpol) from the user-profile AppData path. This additive coverage targets the file-access stage rather than command-line invocation alone."
    mitre_tactic    = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1555.004"
    mitre_technique_name = "Credentials from Password Stores: Windows Credential Manager"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR or Sysmon file-read/open telemetry (Sysmon Event ID 11/15 or EDR equivalent) and process-launch telemetry. Both must be normalised to UDM FILE_READ or FILE_CREATION and PROCESS_LAUNCH respectively."
    platform        = "Windows"
    log_source      = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Backup agents that archive user profiles, credential-sync tools (e.g. enterprise SSO agents), Windows in-box Credential Backup Wizard, automated IT provisioning scripts."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known-good parent process paths to %global_allowed_credmgr_parents. Add authorised backup or sync process paths to %global_allowed_vault_readers. Narrow the file-read event further by requiring the reading process to be non-system (exclude lsass.exe, svchost.exe) if your EDR surfaces that field reliably."

  events:
    // --- Leg 1: Vault enumeration via a process launch ---
    $enum.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_LAUNCH"
    (
      $enum.target.process.file.full_path = /\\vaultcmd\.exe$/ nocase
      or
      (
        $enum.target.process.file.full_path = /\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/ nocase
        and
        $enum.target.process.command_line = /(PasswordVault|CredentialManager|vaultcmd|Credential.*Locker|Windows\.Security\.Credentials)/ nocase
      )
    )
    not $enum.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_credmgr_parents
    $enum.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // --- Leg 2: Direct file access to vault credential or policy files ---
    $vread.metadata.event_type = "FILE_READ"
    $vread.target.file.full_path = /\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\(Vault|Credentials)\\.*\.(vcrd|vpol)$/  nocase
    not $vread.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_vault_readers
    $vread.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // --- Chronological ordering: enumeration must precede file access ---
    $enum.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $vread.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname over 10m

  outcome:
    $risk_score          = max(85)
    $mitre_technique_id  = array_distinct("T1555.004")
    $primary_entity      = array_distinct($hostname)
    $enum_process        = array_distinct($enum.target.process.file.full_path)
    $enum_cmdline        = array_distinct($enum.target.process.command_line)
    $vault_files_accessed = array_distinct($vread.target.file.full_path)
    $reading_process     = array_distinct($vread.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $affected_user       = array_distinct($vread.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $enum and $vread
}

rule MSSP_T1555_005_Password_Manager_DB_File_Read {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Single-Event"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects file-read or file-open access to common Linux password manager database files (KeePass .kdbx, pass store, Bitwarden vault, KWallet, GNOME Keyring, 1Password local vaults). An adversary who has obtained a shell will attempt to stage or exfiltrate the encrypted database as a prerequisite to offline cracking or in-memory decryption. This rule fires on the resulting FILE_READ artifact rather than on the process command line, providing a complementary detection layer that is harder to evade."
    mitre_tactic    = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1555.005"
    mitre_technique_name = "Credentials from Password Stores: Password Managers"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires Linux EDR or auditd with file-read/open syscall auditing enabled (auditd rules: -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S open,openat,read -F exit=-EACCES or equivalent). Chronicle UDM FILE_READ events must be populated with target.file.full_path."
    platform        = "Linux"
    log_source      = "linux_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Legitimate user unlocking their own password manager interactively; backup agents (e.g. rsync, Bacula, Veeam) archiving home directories; secret-scanning CI/CD jobs; password manager auto-save/sync daemons (e.g. keepassxc, pass, rbw). Tune by adding known backup service accounts and approved process paths to the reference lists."
    tuning_guidance = "Add authorised backup or sync process paths to %linux_allowed_pwmgr_readers. Add service accounts that legitimately access vault files to %linux_allowed_pwmgr_users. Consider narrowing the rule to reads originating from processes outside the password manager's own binary (e.g. exclude keepassxc reading its own database)."

  events:
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_READ"

    // Target: common Linux password manager database / vault file extensions and paths.
    // KeePass/KeePassXC (.kdbx), pass (GPG-encrypted files under .password-store),
    // Bitwarden CLI local vault (data.json), KWallet (.kwl), GNOME Keyring (.keyring),
    // 1Password local vault (.1pif / .agilekeychain / .opvault), Enpass (.enpassdb),
    // Dashlane local backup (.dash / .dashlane), generic .vault files.
    (
      $file.target.file.full_path = /\.kdbx$/ nocase
      or $file.target.file.full_path = /\.kwl$/ nocase
      or $file.target.file.full_path = /\.keyring$/ nocase
      or $file.target.file.full_path = /\.1pif$/ nocase
      or $file.target.file.full_path = /\.agilekeychain/ nocase
      or $file.target.file.full_path = /\.opvault/ nocase
      or $file.target.file.full_path = /\.enpassdb$/ nocase
      or $file.target.file.full_path = /\.dash$/ nocase
      or $file.target.file.full_path = /\/\.password-store\// nocase
      or $file.target.file.full_path = /\/\.local\/share\/keyrings\// nocase
      or $file.target.file.full_path = /\/\.config\/Bitwarden\/data\.json$/ nocase
      or $file.target.file.full_path = /\/\.config\/1Password\// nocase
      or $file.target.file.full_path = /\/\.gnome2\/keyrings\// nocase
      or $file.target.file.full_path = /\/kwalletd\// nocase
    )

    // Exclude the password manager's own process reading its own database
    // (normal unlock operation). Attackers use unrelated processes.
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\/(keepassxc|keepass2|keepass|kwalletd5|kwalletd|gnome-keyring-daemon|1password|bitwarden|rbw|pass|gpg|gpg2|gpg-agent)$/ nocase

    // Exclude known authorised backup / sync processes and approved readers.
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %linux_allowed_pwmgr_readers

    // Exclude authorised service accounts (e.g. backup agents).
    not $file.principal.user.userid in %linux_allowed_pwmgr_users

  outcome:
    $risk_score        = max(80)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1555.005")
    $primary_entity    = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)
    $accessing_process = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $vault_file        = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $acting_user       = array_distinct($file.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $file
}

rule MSSP_T1555_005_PasswordMgr_FileRead_Then_ProcOpen {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects a non-password-manager process opening or reading a password-manager database file, followed within 10 minutes by that same process opening a handle to another process (potential credential dumping from memory). Covers KeePass (.kdbx), 1Password (.agilekeychain / .opvault), Bitwarden, and similar flat-file vaults stored on disk. This is additive to process-launch / command-line rules because it focuses on file-access and cross-process handle activity rather than child-process creation."
    mitre_tactic    = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1555.005"
    mitre_technique_name = "Credentials from Password Stores: Password Managers"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires EDR file-read telemetry (FILE_READ events on .kdbx / vault files) and PROCESS_OPEN telemetry. Both are produced by CrowdStrike Falcon, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, SentinelOne, and Sysmon (EventID 10 for process open, EventID 11/23 for file access)."
    platform        = "Windows"
    log_source      = "windows_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Backup agents reading password-manager database files; antivirus scanning vault files; authorised password-manager sync utilities; IT asset-management tools enumerating user profile directories."
    tuning_guidance = "Add legitimate backup or sync process paths to %global_allowed_vault_readers. Add authorised security-tool process paths to %global_allowed_proc_openers. Narrow the file path regex if only specific password managers are in scope."

  events:
    // Leg 1: a suspicious process reads a password-manager database file.
    // We exclude the password-manager's own process to avoid self-access FPs.
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_READ"
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\.(kdbx|kdb|agilekeychain|opvault|dashlane|psafe3|pwsafe|enpass|1pif|bwdb)$/  nocase
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\\(keepass|keeweb|1password|bitwarden|dashlane|roboform|lastpass|enpass|passwordsafe|pwsafe).*\.exe$/  nocase
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_vault_readers
    $file.principal.hostname = $hostname
    $file.principal.process.file.full_path = $reader_proc

    // Leg 2: within the window, the SAME process path opens a handle to
    // another process — indicative of memory-scraping for decrypted credentials.
    $open.metadata.event_type = "PROCESS_OPEN"
    $open.principal.process.file.full_path = $reader_proc
    not $open.principal.process.file.full_path in %global_allowed_proc_openers
    $open.principal.hostname = $hostname

    // Chronological ordering: file read must precede the process-open attempt.
    $file.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $open.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $hostname, $reader_proc over 10m

  outcome:
    $risk_score          = max(85)
    $mitre_technique_id  = array_distinct("T1555.005")
    $primary_entity      = array_distinct($hostname)
    $vault_files_accessed = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $target_processes_opened = array_distinct($open.target.process.file.full_path)
    $suspicious_reader   = array_distinct($reader_proc)
    $event_count         = count($open.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds)

  condition:
    $file and $open
}

rule MSSP_T1555_006_SecretsManager_BulkAccess_After_Login {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Sequence"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects a cloud identity that authenticates (or assumes a role) and then performs repeated secret-retrieval operations against a cloud secrets manager within a short window. A single read is normal; a burst of reads across multiple secrets after a fresh authentication is a strong indicator of credential harvesting from the secrets store."
    mitre_tactic    = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1555.006"
    mitre_technique_name = "Credentials from Password Stores: Cloud Secrets Management Stores"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires cloud provider audit logs normalised into Chronicle UDM. Covers AWS CloudTrail (GetSecretValue, AssumeRole), Azure Activity (KeyVault secret GET), and GCP Audit (accessSecretVersion). Both USER_LOGIN and USER_RESOURCE_ACCESS events must be ingested."
    platform        = "IaaS"
    log_source      = "cloud_audit"
    false_positives = "Automated deployment pipelines that retrieve multiple secrets at startup; secret-rotation Lambda/Cloud Functions; CI/CD service accounts; infrastructure-as-code tooling (Terraform, Pulumi) during plan/apply cycles."
    tuning_guidance = "Add known automation service-account identities to %cloud_secrets_allowed_principals. Raise the threshold in the match window or add a target.resource.name filter to scope to sensitive secret namespaces only."

  events:
    // Event 1: fresh authentication or role assumption into the cloud control plane
    $auth.metadata.event_type = "USER_LOGIN"
    $auth.principal.user.userid != ""
    not $auth.principal.user.userid in %cloud_secrets_allowed_principals

    // Event 2: secret retrieval from a cloud secrets manager
    // Matches AWS GetSecretValue, GCP accessSecretVersion, Azure key-vault secret reads
    // as normalised by Chronicle UDM
    $access.metadata.event_type = "USER_RESOURCE_ACCESS"
    $access.target.resource.resource_type = "CREDENTIAL"
    $access.metadata.description = /secret|secretversion|keyvault.*secret|get.?secret|access.?secret/ nocase
    not $access.principal.user.userid in %cloud_secrets_allowed_principals

    // Join on the same cloud identity across both events
    $auth.principal.user.userid = $actor
    $access.principal.user.userid = $actor

    // Enforce chronological ordering: login must precede secret access
    $auth.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $access.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $actor over 10m

  outcome:
    $risk_score          = max(80)
    $mitre_technique_id  = array_distinct("T1555.006")
    $primary_entity      = array_distinct($actor)
    $secrets_accessed    = array_distinct($access.target.resource.name)
    $secret_access_count = count($access.target.resource.name)
    $source_ips          = array_distinct($access.principal.ip)
    $auth_source_ip      = array_distinct($auth.principal.ip)
    $cloud_project       = array_distinct($access.target.resource.attribute.labels.key)

  condition:
    $auth and $access
}

rule MSSP_T1555_001_Password_Store_File_Read_Linux {
  meta:
    author          = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type       = "Single-Event"
    severity        = "High"
    description     = "Detects file-read or open events targeting common Linux password store paths such as browser credential databases, keyring files, KeePass databases, and application secret stores. This catches credential harvesting at the file-artifact layer rather than the command-line layer, providing additive coverage over process-creation rules."
    mitre_tactic    = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1555"
    mitre_technique_name = "Credentials from Password Stores"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires Linux EDR or auditd with file-open/read syscall auditing enabled (e.g., auditd rules watching -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S open,openat -F exit=-EACCES or equivalent EDR file telemetry). Chronicle UDM FILE_READ or FILE_CREATION events must be populated with target.file.full_path."
    platform        = "Linux"
    log_source      = "linux_endpoint"
    false_positives = "Legitimate password manager GUI applications (e.g., KeePassXC, Seahorse) opened by the owning user; browser processes reading their own profile databases; backup agents archiving home directories; security scanners; secret-scanning CI/CD jobs."
    tuning_guidance = "Add trusted process paths (e.g., keepassxc, gnome-keyring-daemon, backup agents) to %linux_allowed_credential_readers. Scope further by correlating principal.user.userid against the file owner to suppress self-access. Consider raising severity when the accessing process is an interpreter (python, perl, ruby, sh) rather than a known password manager binary."

  events:
    $file.metadata.event_type = "FILE_READ"

    // Target common Linux password store file paths using regex patterns.
    // Covers: Firefox/Chromium/Chrome NSS key databases and logins JSON,
    //         GNOME Keyring files, KWallet, KeePass databases,
    //         libsecret/pass store, SSH private keys in non-standard locations,
    //         .netrc, .pgpass, and generic credential cache files.
    $file.target.file.full_path = /\/(\.mozilla\/firefox\/[^\/]+\/(key[34]\.db|logins\.json|cert[89]\.db)|\.config\/google-chrome\/[^\/]+\/(Login Data|Cookies)|\.config\/chromium\/[^\/]+\/(Login Data|Cookies)|\.local\/share\/keyrings\/[^\/]*\.(keyring|keystore)|\.kde[45]?\/share\/apps\/kwallet\/[^\/]+\.kwl|\.config\/KDE\/[^\/]+\.kwl|\.password-store\/.*\.gpg|\.keepass\/.*\.(kdbx?|kdb)|\.gnupg\/secring\.gpg|\.netrc|\.pgpass|\.aws\/credentials|\.config\/gcloud\/.*credentials.*|\.azure\/.*credentials.*|proc\/[0-9]+\/mem)$/ nocase

    // Exclude the process reading its own legitimate credential file
    // (e.g., the browser reading its own profile). Tuned via reference list.
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path in %linux_allowed_credential_readers

    // Exclude root-owned system maintenance processes that legitimately
    // traverse home directories (backup, indexing daemons).
    not $file.principal.process.file.full_path = /\/(bacula|amanda|rsync|updatedb|mlocate|tracker)/ nocase

  outcome:
    $risk_score        = max(75)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1555")
    $primary_entity    = array_distinct($file.principal.hostname)
    $accessing_process = array_distinct($file.principal.process.file.full_path)
    $target_file       = array_distinct($file.target.file.full_path)
    $accessing_user    = array_distinct($file.principal.user.userid)

  condition:
    $file
}

rule MSSP_T1555_002_Cloud_Secret_Bulk_Access_Then_Exfil_Attempt {
  meta:
    author = "TELUS Automated Detection Pipeline"
    rule_type = "Sequence"
    severity = "High"
    description = "Detects a principal performing bulk access to cloud secrets/password store resources (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, GCP Secret Manager) followed by a resource permissions change or policy modification within a short window. This pattern is consistent with credential harvesting from cloud-native password stores: enumerate secrets, then modify permissions to maintain access or exfiltrate credentials."
    mitre_tactic = "Credential Access"
    mitre_technique = "T1555"
    mitre_technique_name = "Credentials from Password Stores"
    log_prerequisites = "Requires cloud provider audit logs normalised into Chronicle UDM. AWS CloudTrail (GetSecretValue, ListSecrets, PutResourcePolicy), Azure Activity (Key Vault secret reads, access policy updates), or GCP Audit (accessSecretVersion, setIamPolicy) must be ingested."
    platform = "IaaS"
    log_source = "cloud_audit"
    false_positives = "Automated secret rotation pipelines, CI/CD systems retrieving secrets at deploy time, infrastructure-as-code tooling (Terraform, Pulumi) applying permission changes, backup and compliance scanning services."
    tuning_guidance = "Add approved service account identities to %cloud_allowed_secret_automation_principals. Add approved resource name patterns to %cloud_allowed_secret_resources. Raise the threshold count or tighten the time window if CI/CD pipelines generate excessive noise."

  events:
    // Event 1: Principal accesses one or more secrets/password-store resources
    $access.metadata.event_type = "USER_RESOURCE_ACCESS"
    $access.target.resource.type = /secret|vault|kms|key.?vault|secret.?manager|parameter.?store/ nocase
    not $access.principal.user.userid in %cloud_allowed_secret_automation_principals
    not $access.target.resource.name in %cloud_allowed_secret_resources
    $access.principal.user.userid = $actor

    // Event 2: Same principal modifies permissions or policy on any resource shortly after
    $perm.metadata.event_type = "RESOURCE_PERMISSIONS_CHANGE"
    not $perm.principal.user.userid in %cloud_allowed_secret_automation_principals
    $perm.principal.user.userid = $actor

    // Chronological ordering: secret access must precede the permission change
    $access.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= $perm.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds

  match:
    $actor over 10m

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(80)
    $mitre_technique_id = array_distinct("T1555")
    $primary_entity = array_distinct($access.principal.user.userid)
    $accessed_secret_resources = array_distinct($access.target.resource.name)
    $permission_changed_resources = array_distinct($perm.target.resource.name)
    $source_ips = array_distinct($access.principal.ip)
    $access_event_count = count($access.metadata.id)
    $perm_event_count = count($perm.metadata.id)

  condition:
    $access and $perm
}
